false_positives.candidate:
Buffer glossary still calls segment keys complete sets

The glossary still says span-buf:s:* keys are Redis sets containing every span payload for a segment. They are now sorted sets written with ZADD and read with ZSCAN, and ZPOPMIN drops payloads once a segment exceeds 1000 spans, so the key is neither a set nor a complete segment. The algorithm notes above still describe merging sets and never mention eviction. Following the docstring leads operators to set commands (WRONGTYPE) and to treat a flushed segment as complete.

No coverage for eviction, score order, or duplicate ingest

The insert-time cap is the point of this change, but every buffer test still inserts four spans that share end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0 and only checks flushed span ids. Those assertions still pass if ZPOPMIN never runs, if it drops the wrong members, if a second process_spans of the same payloads inflates ZUNIONSTORE scores, or if a segment larger than 1000 spans is returned in full. Add a case with more than 1000 distinctly scored spans (lowest scores removed, segment span kept) and a case that processes the same payloads twice.

Over-cap eviction is silent, ignores config, and can drop the root

If the segment sorted set has more than 1000 members, ZPOPMIN deletes the lowest end_timestamp_precise scores and throws the members away. The limit is hardcoded and does not read SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans (default 1001), which is now unused: the flush path that enforced it, logged the span count, and incremented spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded was removed. Dropped spans are not metered and not marked on the flushed payload, and the consumer still commits the Kafka offset, so the loss is permanent and invisible. There is also no exception for the segment span, so a root whose timestamp is among the lowest is deleted while the has-root-span flag can still be set and a partial segment is emitted as a normal one. Equal scores, which the tests all use, make ZPOPMIN break ties by raw payload bytes, so which spans survive is arbitrary. Pass max_segment_spans into the script, record a metric and a truncation marker, and do not evict the segment span.

Parent-redirect walk cap reduced from 10000 to 1000

The loop that follows span-buf:sr redirects used to run to 10000, with a comment that a deeper chain would not be joined onto the correct segment. It is now for i = 0, 1000 and the warning is gone. This limit is not the eviction cap: it is how many parent hops are resolved to compute set_span_id. A chain longer than 1000 spans, which the old code explicitly tolerated up to 10k and which large traces can produce when batches arrive one level at a time, stops at an intermediate parent. Those spans are merged into the wrong segment key and flushed apart from their root. Restore the previous bound unless there is a measured reason to lower it.

Segment keys changed from SET to ZSET with no migration

Span segment keys stay at span-buf:s:{project:trace}:span_id, but this write switched from SADD to ZADD, add-buffer.lua switched from SCARD/SUNIONSTORE to ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE, and _load_segment_data switched from SSCAN to ZSCAN. Redis raises WRONGTYPE when those commands hit the other type. TTL is 3600s and unflushed segments live at least until the 10s/60s flush. A rolling deploy runs both versions on the same keys, and after cutover leftover SET keys cannot be updated or scanned. process_spans then errors on every retry of that batch and can stall the partition until the key expires; flush_segments fails the same way, so those spans are never emitted. Version the key prefix or dual-handle existing sets before deploying.

ZUNIONSTORE sums scores and breaks redelivery

The merge calls ZUNIONSTORE with no AGGREGATE, so Redis defaults to SUM. Members are the raw span payloads and scores are end_timestamp_precise. Kafka delivery is at-least-once: a retry ZADDs the same payload into the parent key and this script unions that key into the segment key that already holds the member. Each retry adds the timestamp again (T, 2T, 3T). The previous SUNIONSTORE path was idempotent. After the new 1000-span cap, ZPOPMIN keeps the inflated duplicates and drops spans that were ingested only once. Under the cap every member is still present, so the existing flush tests do not catch it. Pass AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN) so a retry keeps a real timestamp.

true_positives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Test events store the client sample rate, not an upsample weight

`_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` runs on every `store_event` and, when `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` is truthy, overwrites `normalized_data["sample_rate"]` with that raw rate. It never sets `sample_weight` and never stores `1/client_sample_rate`. The new stats test saves `client_sample_rate: 0.1` and expects `count == 10`, while `upsampled_count` in discover.py aggregates `sum(sample_weight)`. Nothing in this PR connects those: production ingest is unchanged, and this hook does not invert the rate. Unless an out-of-diff pipeline already materializes `sample_weight` as `1/sample_rate` from the event `sample_rate` field, allowlisted `count()` queries error on an unknown column or return a non-upsampled value, and the new snuba test cannot pass. The hook also swallows all exceptions, ignores a falsy rate via `if client_sample_rate`, and can clobber an existing server `sample_rate` on any other test event that includes that context.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling uses the outer dataset and request query, not the query executed

`_get_event_stats` decides upsampling by calling `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` with the closed-over `dataset` and `request`, ignoring the `scoped_dataset` and `query` arguments it actually runs. Dashboard discover-split rewrites those arguments: error probes use discover and `({query}) AND !event.type:transaction`, transaction probes add `event.type:transaction`, and the outer dataset is often metrics-enhanced performance, which `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` always rejects. The helper only looks at `request.GET["query"]`, so every probe inherits the original request's decision. A transaction probe whose original query contains `event.type:error` is still rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)` and comes back empty or errors; `check_if_results_have_data` then reports no transactions and `save_split_decision` persists that on `DashboardWidget.discover_widget_split`. Later loads skip the check and keep the wrong split. Error-only split queries whose original request text did not contain `event.type:error` are never upsampled. Pass the executed dataset and query string into the check. The outer `except Exception` retry calls `_get_event_stats` again, so a Snuba failure from the rewrite is not avoided and surfaces as a 500 (the endpoint only catches `ValidationError`).

false_negatives.golden_comment: Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

false_positives.candidate:
Allowlist cache is slower than options.get and cannot be invalidated

Every organization events-stats request now does a default-cache get (Redis in production) under `error_upsampling_eligible:{org}:{hash(sorted(project_ids))}`, and a set on miss, to avoid `options.get("issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist")`. That option read is already process-local memory, so this adds a network round trip and a high-cardinality key (one entry per distinct project-id set) on a hot endpoint. The cached boolean does not include the allowlist version. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called, and it can delete only one project-set key, so an allowlist edit cannot drop the other combinations. For up to 60 seconds after a project is removed, stats keep rewriting `count()` to `sum(sample_weight)` and can 500 or return weighted counts for projects that are no longer eligible; after a project is added, counts stay raw. The note on `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` says the allowlist is read fresh on every call so config changes apply immediately, which is false once this cache is in front. Read the option directly, or cache it in-process keyed by the allowlist contents and actually invalidate it.

Error-query check is a substring match and false-positives on negation

`_is_error_focused_query` lowercases `request.GET["query"]` and returns true when the substring `event.type:error` appears anywhere. That is true for `!event.type:error`, for `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, and for a quoted value such as `message:"event.type:error"`. On an allowlisted project set those queries rewrite `count()` to `sum(sample_weight)`. Non-error rows do not have a usable weight, so the stats request undercounts (NULLs add nothing) or fails in Snuba. The same check misses the usual discover error filter `!event.type:transaction` and list syntax such as `event.type:[error]`, so those error queries stay at the raw sampled count. The unit tests only cover the exact strings `event.type:error` and `event.type:transaction`, so the negation false positive is untested. Parse the search query and honor negation instead of substring matching.

Top-events ranking, equations, and count filters are not upsampled

Only the y-axis list is rewritten, and `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` replaces a column only when the entire string is `count()` after strip and lower. `top_events_timeseries` still gets `selected_columns` from `get_field_list`, `equations` from `get_equation_list`, and `orderby` from `get_orderby`, plus the raw `user_query`. Top-N is therefore ranked by sampled `count()` while the series uses `upsampled_count() as count`, so a heavily sampled group can be dropped from the top N, and an orderby that still names `count()` can fail the query because that aggregate was renamed. Aggregate conditions such as `count():>10` in the user query stay raw. Equation y-axes (`equation|count() / count_unique(user)`), `count() as <alias>`, `epm()`, and `eps()` are not rewritten either, so one response can mix upsampled and sampled series. Rewrite every count-based aggregate the query will run, or refuse those shapes while upsampling is on.

Transaction upsampling test queries before the event is ingested

`test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events` calls `store_event` for a transaction and immediately GETs events-stats. `setUp` has to call `wait_for_event_count` before its queries, so ingestion is asynchronous here. The assertion that the first bucket `count` is 1 races the consumer and flakes at 0. Waiting for `wait_for_event_count(self.project.id, 1)` would also be wrong: `setUp` already stored an error in that project, so a count of 1 is satisfied before the transaction is written. Wait until that transaction is actually queryable (for example project event count 2, or a transaction-specific query) before asserting.

Upsampled count drops events with no weight and truncates

`upsampled_count` is `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`, and the helper comment says null checks are intentionally omitted. ClickHouse `sum` skips NULLs, so any error in an allowlisted project that has no `sample_weight` (historical events, events ingested before the column was filled, or unsampled events that should count as 1) contributes nothing. Enabling the allowlist can therefore make the series smaller than raw `count()`, including showing 0. `toInt64` truncates toward zero, so a fractional weight such as `1/0.3` is biased low on every bucket (one event at 3.333 becomes 3). If `sample_weight` is actually the rate 0.1 rather than the multiplier 10, `toInt64(sum(...))` is 0, not the 10 the new test expects. The aggregate needs a missing-weight default of 1 and rounding (for example `round(sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1)))`). With that default, mixed queries would not need the all-or-nothing allowlist gate, which today changes a project's displayed count depending on whether every other selected project is allowlisted.

Upsampling stats tests share one cache key and disagree on the allowlist

These tests patch `sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options` but not `sentry.utils.cache.cache`. Eligibility is cached for 60 seconds under a key built only from organization id and the project id set. All four tests use the same projects, so they share that key, while stubbing three different allowlists (both ids, one id, and empty) and expecting different counts (10 vs 1). This class's `setUp` never calls `cache.clear()` or deletes that key, and Django's `TestCase` does not clear the cache. If an earlier test cached true, `test_error_upsampling_with_partial_allowlist` and `test_error_upsampling_with_no_allowlisted_projects` still rewrite `count()` and their `count == 1` assertions fail; the reverse order makes the allowlisted test expect 10 and get 1. Mock or clear the cache in `setUp`.

errors dataset always rewrites count() but the function is only added on discover

`_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns true for any `sentry.snuba.errors` query, and the endpoint then sends `upsampled_count()` to that dataset's query builder. The aggregate is only inserted into discover.py's `function_converter`. `sentry.search.events.builder.errors` is not changed, and `OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest` never passes `dataset=errors` (it uses the default dataset plus `query=event.type:error`). If the errors dataset does not inherit Discover's function map, every allowlisted `dataset=errors` stats request fails with an unknown function as soon as the allowlist is non-empty. The string-level unit test does not run the query builder, so it would not catch that. Register the function on the errors dataset config and add a snuba test that uses `dataset=errors`.

upsampled_count is public, so the allowlist does not gate the feature

The new `SnQLFunction` is registered without `private=True`, unlike the internal aggregate immediately above it. The allowlist logic only rewrites a y-axis that is exactly `count()`; it does not block callers from requesting the function themselves. Any client can pass `yAxis=upsampled_count()` on discover and bypass the rollout. On datasets or projects where `sample_weight` is absent (transactions, spans, non-allowlisted projects) that same public function turns a user-controlled y-axis into a failed stats query. The aggregate should stay internal to the rewrite path so the allowlist is actually what enables it.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Error context is paired by dict order, not event id

fetch_error_details builds node ids from error_ids, then does zip(error_ids, events.values()) on the dict returned by nodestore.backend.get_multi. That pairs by iteration order, not by node id. Backends that omit missing keys (the usual get_multi behavior) shift every later row: if the second id is absent, the third event's title, message, and timestamp are attached to the second id and the last id is dropped. The id field is not even used in the log line, so the Seer prompt gets the wrong errors and timestamps. The new test only stores one error, so it cannot catch this. Look up each node id in the dict instead of zipping values().

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Flagged table widgets render an empty table instead of query results

When organization.features includes use-table-widget-visualization, WidgetCardChart replaces StyledSimpleTableChart with TableWidgetVisualization passed columns={[]} and tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}. The real result.data, result.meta, fields, and loading state are discarded. TableWidgetVisualization only falls back to meta.fields when columns is nullish, so an empty array also suppresses column extraction. Enabling the flag blanks every dashboard table widget (including during load) instead of showing the query.

true_positives.golden_comment: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Report age/timestamp rules do not match the spec the serializer claims

age and timestamp are both required=False, and there is no object-level validate() requiring exactly one of them. A report with neither is accepted and counted. The field validators also use initial_data.get("age") / get("timestamp"), which treat 0 as absent, so a report with age=0 and timestamp=0 skips both mutual-exclusion checks (0 is a valid age and a valid timestamp). Use "age" in initial_data (and the same for timestamp) and reject payloads that do not have exactly one of the two fields.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

false_positives.candidate:
60s deadline is too short for a 100-identity auth refresh

check_auth_identities now has processing_deadline_duration=60 while it still loops up to chunk_size (default 100) identities, each doing an org-membership RPC and provider.refresh_identity HTTP call. 100 sequential IdP calls routinely exceed 60s, so the taskworker kills the task mid-batch. check_auth already sets last_synced=now on those ids before enqueueing this task, and they are not selected again until the next ~24h window (AUTH_CHECK_INTERVAL). Identities not yet refreshed are skipped for a day, so SSO invalidation is delayed. Raise the deadline to match the chunk, or shrink the chunk to what 60s can finish.

Attribute-key hook returns undefined after a failed fetch

useTraceItemAttributeKeys used to always reduce the API payload to a TagCollection (empty object if data was missing) and return that once loading finished. It now returns useQuery's data directly: attributes is previous while isFetching, otherwise data. On error, isFetching is false and data is undefined, and there is no ?? {}. Explore callers that wait for !isLoading and then spread or Object.keys the result will throw, blanking the search builder, instead of seeing an empty tag set. Return data ?? {} (and keep the previous value only while refetching).

Error and breadcrumb timestamps are not on the same scale

gen_request_data interleaves errors and breadcrumbs with error["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0). Replay segment events are raw rrweb records whose timestamp is epoch milliseconds. fetch_error_details copies the nodestore event timestamp, which is epoch seconds (or sometimes an ISO string). Seconds are always less than millisecond breadcrumbs, so every error is emitted before the first breadcrumb and the summary chronology is wrong for real replays. An ISO-string timestamp raises TypeError on < or sort, and that exception is outside fetch_error_details's try/except, so the summarize request 500s. The new tests hide this by writing segment JSON with now.timestamp() seconds. Normalize both sides to the same numeric unit before comparing.

Error ids are queried with the page stats window, not the replay

Error context now depends on query_replay_instance(start=filter_params["start"], end=filter_params["end"]) from ProjectEndpoint.get_filter_params. The replay AI tab (static/app/views/replays/detail/ai/index.tsx) calls this endpoint with no start, end, or statsPeriod. The lookup therefore uses the generic project default stats window rather than the replay's own start/end. Replays outside that window return no row, error_ids stays empty, and the summary is produced without error context with no error to the user. Query the replay by id over its retention window, or pass the replay bounds from the client.

Feedback list is clipped after the summary is inserted

The list grid cell used to be a FluidHeight Container (height 100% of the stretched grid area). It is now SummaryListContainer, a column flex with no min-height: 0 or overflow handling, containing FeedbackSummary plus that same height-100% Container. The list's 100% height is the full cell, then the summary and gap are added on top, so the column overflows the grid row. Background and LayoutGrid both set overflow: hidden, so the bottom of the feedback list is clipped and no longer lines up with the details pane. Give the list container flex: 1 and min-height: 0 (and overflow: hidden) so it fills only the space under the summary.

Feedback summary ignores the environment page filter

useFeedbackSummary reads usePageFilters().selection and sends normalized datetime plus project, but not selection.environments. The feedback list on the same page is scoped by the environment page filter. With an environment selected, the summary is computed from every environment in the projects and date range, so it can describe feedback the list is not showing. Pass environment (and any other page filters the summary API supports) in the query.

Hidden span attributes are only removed while searching

HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES (is_segment, project_id, received) is applied only inside the searchQuery branch. When the search box is empty the code returns sortAttributes(attributes) unchanged, so those internal fields stay visible. Once the user types a query that would match them, they disappear. If the intent is to hide them, filter them out before the search check; otherwise search results disagree with the full list.

Issue titles are interpolated into markdown links unsanitized

MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE is "* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}\n" and _truncate_title only slices to 50 characters. Issue titles come from user-influenced error messages. A title containing ] or ) breaks out of the link, for example [**click here](https://evil.example)**](real-url), and is posted to GitHub/GitLab. Truncation does not stop that. Escape markdown metacharacters in the title (and backticks in the environment name) before formatting.

Suspect-issue PR comments will crash with AttributeError

get_merged_pr_single_issue_template and get_environment_info were added as methods of CommitContextIntegration, but GitHubPRCommentWorkflow and GitlabPRCommentWorkflow (subclasses of PRCommentWorkflow, which does not inherit CommitContextIntegration) call them as self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...) and self.get_environment_info(issue). That raises AttributeError before a comment body can be built, so merged-PR suspect-issue comments stop being posted. The helper also calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, but _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration, not PRCommentWorkflow, so even a direct call on the integration class fails the same way. The updated GitHub/GitLab comment tests expect the new body and will fail on this AttributeError. Move the helpers onto PRCommentWorkflow (where the callers live) and truncate via that class.

true_positives.golden_comment: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup code comparison is case-sensitive and unnormalized

Codes are generated as lowercase hex (crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex") in setup.ts) and login compares them with indexOf after only stripping "-". The same check is in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts at the backupCode.replaceAll call. There is no toLowerCase() or trim, and spaces are left in place. The recovery input in apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx uses placeholder "XXXXX-XXXXX" and does not set autoCapitalize="none", so mobile keyboards and anyone following the placeholder submit uppercase hex. Those attempts always fail as an incorrect backup code, which blocks the recovery path when the authenticator is already lost. Normalize by trimming, removing dashes and spaces, and lowercasing on the server, and stop advertising uppercase in the field.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
One-time backup codes are consumed with a lost update

Redeeming a backup code decrypts the stored list, finds a match, sets that slot to null, and writes the whole blob back with a plain user.update keyed only by id. There is no transaction, row lock, or compare-and-swap on the previous ciphertext. Two overlapping logins can both read the same list and both succeed: the same code opens two sessions, and if the requests use two different codes the later write restores the code the earlier request consumed. The promise that each code works exactly once is therefore not enforced. Consume the code with a conditional update (or SELECT FOR UPDATE) that fails if backupCodes changed, and only then issue the session.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup-code login skips the password when totpCode is set

Password verification runs only when `user.password` is set and `credentials.totpCode` is empty (the check around line 121). The new backup-code branch then logs the user in if the backup code matches and never validates `totpCode`. A request with the victim's email, any non-empty totpCode (for example "000000"), and a valid backup code therefore skips the password entirely, consumes that code, and creates a session. Backup codes are supposed to replace the authenticator only; the login UI still sends the password and clears totpCode, but the credentials callback must not trust the client to omit totpCode. Anyone who obtains a backup code (the downloaded cal-backup-codes.txt, a screenshot, a clipboard history) can take over the account without the password. Verify the password inside this branch whenever the user has one, and do not treat an unchecked totpCode as proof the password was already accepted.

Closing the codes dialog does not finish 2FA setup

On a successful enable response the modal only moves to DisplayBackupCodes and no longer calls onEnable(). onEnable() runs solely from the footer Close button. Escape, the overlay, and the dialog's default close control go through onOpenChange and do not notify the parent, so the settings switch stays off while twoFactorEnabled is already true on the server. Clicking the switch again calls setup and gets TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled, so the user cannot finish or disable 2FA until a full reload. The codes themselves exist only in component state and a blob URL from the earlier setup response; nothing can fetch or regenerate them. Refreshing, closing the tab, or dismissing the dialog drops the only copy. The copy button makes this worse: navigator.clipboard.writeText is not awaited, and the success toast is shown even if the write fails, so the user can close thinking the codes were saved. Call onEnable() when enable succeeds (and on every close after that), require an explicit save acknowledgement, and do not toast success unless the clipboard write resolves.

Tests never log in or disable 2FA with a backup code

The new coverage only clicks download, copy, and close on the codes screen. Nothing submits a backup code at login, checks that a used code is rejected, or disables 2FA with a backup code (the TODO at the top of this file calls that out). The existing enable-and-login test was not updated for the new screen: after OTP it never clicks backup-codes-close, and expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy() asserts on the Promise returned by isChecked(), which is always truthy, so it passes even when the switch is unchecked. A break in backup-code authentication, including the password bypass and the non-atomic consume, would not fail CI.

missing_backup_codes points at a settings flow that does not exist

The new string says "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." This PR only creates codes inside the initial 2FA setup response and never adds a settings action to generate or rotate them. Users who enabled 2FA before the migration, or who dismissed the one-time codes screen, hit this error on "Lost access" and are told to do something the product cannot do. They can only get codes by disabling 2FA (which still requires the authenticator) and turning it on again. The message should not claim a generate-in-settings flow unless that flow exists.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google Meet bookings crash when no destination calendar is set

The Cal Video fallback now does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no null check. If destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or [], that value is undefined and booking creation throws TypeError before the location can be switched. The old code used optional chaining, so Meet with no Google calendar fell back to Cal Video. Every caller that passes null or [] (new bookings with no destination calendar, confirmation, and payment webhooks) will 500 on Google Meet instead of booking.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google update/delete fallback can never resolve a calendar id

updateEvent now does `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`. When externalCalendarId is null, undefined, or empty, the find compares every calendar id to that same falsy value and always returns undefined. The previous fallback was the destination calendar's externalId. calendar.events.update is then called with calendarId undefined and the update fails. deleteEvent (around line 315) uses the same dead find and then substitutes "primary", so a missing externalCalendarId deletes on the primary calendar; a 404 is treated as success and the event remains on the calendar it was actually created on. Any reference stored without externalCalendarId, including the no-credentialId create branch and seated-attendee updates that pass a null externalCalendarId, hits this.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Organization slug condition is inverted

The organization create payload changed `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` into `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. That drops the negation. With billing disabled, neither `slug` nor `requestedSlug` is saved, so the new org has no URL. With billing enabled, `slug` is written immediately and `requestedSlug` is still written, so the slug is claimed before payment instead of staying pending. This is unrelated to destination calendars and will break org creation in both modes.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
One missing host credential fails every calendar update

The new per-reference update loop loads a credential from the DB, but if that row is missing or has no app.slug it still pushes updateEvent(undefined, ...). getCalendar then rejects. Unlike createAllCalendarEvents, there is no `if (credential)` guard. The shared catch (around line 591) also dropped the console.error, and it returns a synthetic failure for every calendar reference instead of the updates that already succeeded. With multiple host references, one deleted or unlinked credential makes reschedule, location change, and attendee updates report total calendar failure and hides the underlying error. The seated-merge delete just below also calls getCalendar on a findUnique result with no null check, so a missing old credential aborts the same way.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
CRM other_calendar references are updated twice

calendar references are now every reference whose type includes `_calendar`. Types such as closecom_other_calendar match that filter, so they are updated in the new per-reference loop and again by the later pass that filters `type.includes("other_calendar")`. Previously find() handled only the first calendar reference, and the second pass was what updated CRM calendars. Duplicate updates can create duplicate CRM activities or fail the second call. The first loop should exclude other_calendar types.

Cancelling remaining recurring bookings does not delete each host event

The new per-reference cancel loop wraps the recurring all-remaining branch unchanged. That branch ignores the reference it is iterating, loads only booking.user.credentials (the organizer, not other hosts, and with no DB lookup), and for each future instance deletes only the first reference whose type includes `_calendar`. Other hosts' events on those instances are never deleted, so their calendars keep the cancelled series. Because this sits inside the new for-loop, the same incomplete delete also runs once per calendar reference and hammers the first event. The non-recurring branch already deletes each reference with its own credentialId and a DB fallback; the recurring branch needs the same treatment over every updated instance's calendar references.

Collective host calendars are dropped when the organizer has none

Team destination calendars are collected for COLLECTIVE hosts, then attached with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)`. The evt is initialized to null when both the event type and the organizer have no destination calendar, so the optional push is a no-op and those host calendars are discarded. createAllCalendarEvents then takes the empty branch, whose fallback filters credentials with `type === "calendar"`. Real types are `google_calendar` and similar, so that fallback never matches either. A collective booking whose organizer has not set a destination calendar creates no per-host calendar events even when every other host has a calendar connected.

Location updates persist calendar references without ids

updateLocation now sets externalCalendarId from result.externalId and credentialId from result.credentialId only. CalendarManager.updateEvent does not return either field, and the previous fallbacks to evt.destinationCalendar.externalId and credentialId were removed. editLocation writes referencesToCreate onto the booking. Calendar update results have updatedEvent rather than createdEvent, so those new rows also get uid "". A later cancel treats them as legacy references and calls deleteEvent with an empty uid on every calendar credential, and the real calendar id needed to patch the existing event is gone.

No test covers multi-host calendar create or cancel

This change rewrites create, update, and delete across every destination calendar, but the only test edit is an e2e webhook expectation for an empty destinationCalendar. There is no coverage that a collective booking writes one event per host credential, that Google Meet with no destination calendar still books, that Office/CalDAV/Apple hosts are not given the organizer's calendar id, or that cancelling all remaining recurring instances deletes every host event. The PR checklist notes that no such tests were added, so these regressions will not be caught before merge.

Payment and confirmation creates still use a single destination calendar

Only handleNewBooking appends the other collective hosts' destination calendars. Stripe payment_intent.succeeded calls EventManager.create with an evt whose destinationCalendar is at most `[booking.destinationCalendar || user.destinationCalendar]`. The same single-calendar evt is built in getBooking (used by setup_intent.succeeded around the eventManager.create call) and in paypal-webhook.ts handlePaymentSuccess. confirm.handler.ts builds the same one-element list from the booking relation or the session user and passes it to handleConfirmation, without loading event-type hosts. Booking.destinationCalendar can store only the first calendar (handleNewBooking connects evt.destinationCalendar[0]). Paid or requires-confirmation collective bookings therefore still create only the organizer's calendar event, so the other hosts never get invited.

Seat merge deletes only the first host calendar event

When newBookingId is set (rescheduling a seated attendee into an existing slot), the cleanup still does booking.references.find for a single `_calendar` reference and deletes only that event. The rest of this function was rewritten to walk every calendar reference, but this path was not. Other hosts keep a live event at the old time after the merge, so their calendars stay busy and still show the meeting.

Secondary host events are created against the first destination calendar

createAllCalendarEvents loops over every destination calendar and calls createEvent once per host credential, but it still passes the full destinationCalendar array. CalendarManager.createEvent forwards only credential.id into the service, not that destination's externalId. Office 365, Lark, and CalDAV/Apple all still read only the first array element: Office builds `/me/calendars/${firstExternalId}/events` with the other host's token, Lark creates on the first calendar id, and BaseCalendarService filters to the first externalId. If that id is not on the secondary account, CalDAV's filter matches nothing, Promise.all of an empty list is treated as success, and a booking reference is stored for an event that was never created. Google does look up calendarId by credentialId, but the organizer attendee email is still the first destination's externalId, so the secondary Google insert can 400 or list the wrong organizer. Hosts other than the first therefore do not reliably get a calendar event, which is the bug this PR is meant to fix.

Video booking references no longer store credentialId

referencesToCreate used to set credentialId to result.credentialId for every non-calendar result. It is now `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so video (and any other non-calendar) references are always saved without a credential id. handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when bookingVideoReference.credentialId is set, and then looks that id up in the user's credentials. New bookings will leave Zoom/Daily/other video meetings in place on cancel, and later location updates cannot find the credential that created the meeting.

Webhook destinationCalendar shape changed and is inconsistent

CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from a single DestinationCalendar or null to an array or null, and that object is spread into webhook payloads. Subscribers reading destinationCalendar.integration or destinationCalendar.externalId will break, but the PR is marked as a non-breaking bug fix. Emitters also disagree on the empty value: handleNewBooking still sends null when no calendar is set, while confirm, cancel, reminders, and payment handlers send []. The e2e suite only changed BOOKING_REJECTED to expect [] and still expects null for BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED, so the new contract is neither documented nor consistently tested.

Office 365 calendar then spreads tokenResponse.data onto the stored credential and writes it (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts around line 264). Microsoft often omits refresh_token on refresh and expects the previous one to be kept; the Office 365 schema marks it optional for that reason. The next refresh sends grant refresh_token=refresh_token, Microsoft returns invalid_grant, and the connection stays dead until the user reconnects. In sync mode the minimum schema strips the real refresh_token first, so this always fires, and Zoom then saves that literal (zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts line 120) in place of the real refresh token.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:

minimumTokenResponseSchema is used whenever credential sync and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set. The computed keys z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString() are not Zod wildcards; both become "[object Object]", so the second overwrites the first. The schema only requires access_token and z.object strips unknown keys by default (there is no passthrough). Expiry, refresh_token, scope, and instance_url are discarded. Office 365, Zoom, and Salesforce then persist that stripped object. Zoom also sets expiry_date from the missing expires_in, which becomes NaN. A sync refresh therefore corrupts the stored credential instead of updating it.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

That helper returns the Zod safeParse result {success: true, data: {...}}, not the token object (Office 365 and Zoom read .data). The next GoogleCalendarService constructor runs googleCredentialSchema.parse on that wrapper, which no longer has access_token at the top level, and throws. This runs whenever the access token is expiring, including when credential sync is disabled, so existing Google Calendar connections break until the user reconnects. If the Prisma write throws, the catch treats any error other than invalid_grant as recoverable and returns the old client, so the new token is never stored either.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. true_positives.golden_comment: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

The update path writes only key and does not set invalid to false. Google, Webex, and Zoom set invalid after invalid_grant and then skip that credential. If a self-hoster pushes a fresh key for that user, this endpoint still returns 200, but Cal.com keeps ignoring the row, so the integration stays disconnected until the flag is cleared or the user reinstalls the app.

The handler uses findFirst and then updates or creates, with no transaction, lock, or unique constraint on (userId, appId). userId and type are not unique on Credential (other OAuth callbacks already special-case duplicates). Two deliveries for the same user and app, including a retry, can both see no row and both insert. findFirst has no orderBy, so a later sync updates an arbitrary duplicate while calendar code that also uses findFirst can keep the stale key. The user ends up with two credentials and the integration may keep using outdated tokens.

refreshAccessToken still deletes the credential and throws when the local refresh token is missing or refresh_expires_date has passed, and that check runs before refreshOAuthTokens. With credential sync enabled, the parent app holds the real tokens and the local refresh token may be expired or absent, which is exactly when the sync endpoint should be called. Instead the row is deleted, the sync URL is never hit, and the user must reconnect Lark. The sync branch has to run before this destructive local-token check.

The PR checklist says tests were not added and were not run. The sync-disabled path needs a test that a provider response without refresh_token does not overwrite the stored refresh token and that credential.key is the token object, not a Zod safeParse wrapper. Without that, the credential corruption in parseRefreshTokenResponse and Google CalendarService is not caught before deploy.

The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug. It does not send CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, a signature, or an Authorization header, and it does not check response.ok. The inbound webhook that writes credentials requires the shared secret, but the call that returns live access tokens does not prove it came from this Cal.com instance. An endpoint implemented to match this client cannot tell Cal.com from any other caller, so anyone who can reach that URL can request access tokens for arbitrary user ids and app slugs.

Salesforce refresh calls prisma without importing it

The new getClient path calls prisma.credential.update after exchanging the refresh token, but this file never imports prisma. Reaching that line throws ReferenceError: prisma is not defined and fails typecheck. getClient runs from the SalesforceCalendarService constructor, so every Salesforce create, update, or availability check throws and no connection is returned. Salesforce refreshes the OAuth token on every client construction

getClient always POSTs to the Salesforce token endpoint before building the connection, with no check that the stored access token is still valid. Availability and booking construct SalesforceCalendarService often, so each call adds a token round trip and consumes Salesforce OAuth quota. Previously the connection was created from the stored token and jsforce refreshed only when Salesforce rejected it. A sync or refresh using one of these strings will not find the credential written under the other, so Zoom tokens will not update, or a second credential will be created under the wrong slug and never used by the video adapter.

A blocked address with different casing, or a blacklist entry with a leading space after the comma, is stored and emailed. The read of existing attendees is also outside a transaction, so two parallel requests can both pass the filter and insert the same guest. If isTeamAdmin matches only ADMIN, the check is always false; if it also treats OWNER as admin, only owners pass and admins still fail. If the request includes someone already on the booking plus a new guest, the existing person is not inserted again but still gets a fresh scheduled email and does not get the guests-added notice. Add-guest emails ignore disabled standard emails

sendAddGuestsEmails always emails the organizer and every attendee. Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

Add-guests is offered on past bookings

The new additional-guests action is added to editBookingActions, which is included in bookedActions. bookedActions is not limited to upcoming meetings: past confirmed bookings and past pending bookings also render TableActions with that list. Using it still inserts attendees and sends AttendeeScheduledEmail plus an ICS REQUEST for a time that already passed. Authorization only checks organizer, attendee, or the broken team-admin flag. booking.status, end time, and list size are never validated, and ZAddGuestsInputSchema is an unbounded email array. Any logged-in attendee can therefore add as many addresses as they want to a cancelled, rejected, unconfirmed, or past booking. Each new address is sent AttendeeScheduledEmail, and the mailer hardcodes ICS status CONFIRMED. videoCallData (join URL and meeting password) is copied onto the event whenever a video reference exists, so those invites disclose meeting access for events that are not accepted upcoming meetings, and a participant can send unlimited calendar mail through the platform. EventManager is built from the signed-in user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). Calendar BookingReferences are tied to the organizer's credential id (and other hosts' credentials on collective events), not the caller's. The query already loads booking.user with credentials and destinationCalendar and never uses that user. When an attendee adds guests, the host calendar event is not updated. Load the event-type hosts and set calEvent.team the same way other booking mail flows do.

prisma.booking.update commits the new Attendee rows before translation loading, updateCalendarAttendees, and sendAddGuestsEmails. The calendar call is outside the try/catch, so a thrown calendar or translation error returns 500 after the insert. A retry then filters those addresses out as already present and throws emails_must_be_unique_valid, so the calendar update and invite emails are never retried and the user is told the addresses are invalid. Email failures are caught, logged as a static string with the error discarded, and the handler still returns success, so the dialog toasts Guests added when nobody was notified. New guests are stored with a blank name

Every newly inserted guest is saved with name set to an empty string. Scheduled and add-guest mail payloads address the recipient as `${attendee.name} <${attendee.email}>`, so new guests, who are sent AttendeeScheduledEmail, get a blank display name (` <email>`). The new mutation ships with no unit or integration tests. The inverted team-admin condition, access to cancelled or past bookings, seated overbooking, blacklist casing, and a calendar or email failure after the attendee insert would not be caught in CI. Seated events are not capacity-checked

Guests are inserted as Attendee rows with no comparison to eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot, which is only copied onto the calendar payload later. If occupancy is the attendee count, this overbooks the slot and can block real bookers. If occupancy is BookingSeat / seatsReferences, these guests become attendees with no seat, so seat counts, the seats UI, and cancel/reschedule links diverge from the attendee list. seatsShowAttendees is also ignored: sendAddGuestsEmails and the ICS include every attendee, leaking participant emails on events configured to hide them. Enforce remaining capacity before insert, or reject add-guests for seated events, and honor seatsShowAttendees when emailing.

Failures write retryCount to the in-memory value plus one instead of an atomic increment, and the cleanup delete removes any row with retryCount > 1 even when scheduled is already true. The handler never claims the row before calling Twilio, so overlapping cron runs can interleave: one run fails and stores retryCount 2, while the other run's scheduleSMS succeeds and sets scheduled and referenceId without clearing retryCount. Partial updates do not reset the other field, so the next run deletes that row. The Twilio message stays queued, but the referenceId required to cancel it is gone. Use an atomic increment and only delete unscheduled SMS rows.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Retry cleanup deletes reminders of every method

The new deleteMany ORs the old past-due SMS cleanup with retryCount > 1, and that second predicate has no method, scheduled, or scheduledDate filter. WorkflowReminder is shared by EMAIL, SMS, and WHATSAPP. On the next run of this SMS cron, any row with retryCount greater than 1 is deleted, including email and WhatsApp reminders and SMS rows already marked scheduled with a Twilio referenceId. Deleting a scheduled row drops the referenceId used to cancel the queued text, so a later booking cancellation cannot stop the message. The comment above the query still says it only removes past SMS reminders, which is no longer true. Scope the retry branch to unscheduled SMS (method SMS and scheduled false).

false_positives.candidate:
Missing number or empty body never consumes retries

retryCount is only updated when scheduleSMS returns falsy or throws. If sendTo is missing or the message body is empty, the code skips the send and does not increment retryCount or delete the row. Those reminders stay scheduled=false and are loaded, and their templates rebuilt, on every cron run until scheduledDate is in the past. That is the unbounded retry this PR is meant to stop, for a permanent failure that will never succeed. Treat that skip as a failed attempt or delete the row.

No test locks the retry delete scope or threshold

The PR adds a destructive delete and a failure counter with no tests. Nothing asserts that an email or WhatsApp reminder with retryCount > 1 is kept, that an already scheduled SMS row is kept, that a missing phone number does not spin until the event date, or that an SMS reminder is removed only after two failures and not on the first. Those are the branches this change gets wrong, and a fixture test of the delete filter and the increment paths would have caught them.

Retry-count update in catch aborts the rest of the batch

The new workflowReminder.update inside the per-reminder catch is not guarded. If it throws — the row was already deleted because the booking was cancelled, or the database errors — the exception escapes the catch, the original scheduling error is never logged, and the for-loop stops. Every later reminder in this invocation is skipped. Previously a single reminder failure was logged and the handler continued. If scheduleSMS had already accepted the message and the follow-up update failed, this path also counts that as a retry failure without saving referenceId, so the queued text can no longer be cancelled. The retry update needs its own try/catch so one row cannot fail the batch.

retryCount is incremented both when scheduleSMS returns a falsy value and for every exception in the surrounding try, including template rendering, getBookerBaseUrl, and database lookups, not only Twilio rejections. The next cron then deletes the row once retryCount > 1. Permanent failures (invalid number) and transient ones (Twilio 5xx, rate limit, network, brief DB error) share that budget, with no backoff beyond the cron interval. Two failures close together therefore remove the reminder even if the event is still days away, so a short provider outage can silently drop every SMS reminder in the 7-day window. Only non-retryable errors should exhaust the counter; transient errors need more attempts or a delay before deletion.

retryCount cleanup sequentially scans WorkflowReminder

Every cron invocation deletes rows with retryCount > 1, but the new predicate is not covered by the existing indexes on (method, scheduled, scheduledDate), bookingUid, workflowStepId, seatReferenceId, or (cancelled, scheduledDate). Postgres must sequentially scan WorkflowReminder on each run, even when almost no rows match. On a bookings-scale table that scan is repeated for the life of the cron. Add an index that matches the cleanup filter (for example method plus retryCount) if this delete stays.

This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

OR SQL fragments are unsafe to AND with more predicates

Team and org authorization SQL is an OR of a team-booking predicate and a personal-booking predicate, joined as `(${left}) OR (${right})` in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition. That groups each side only; it does not parenthesize the whole OR. When eventTypeId and memberUserId are absent, getBaseConditions returns that fragment unchanged. SQL binds AND tighter than OR, so a caller query `WHERE ${conditions} AND "startTime" >= ${from}` is parsed as team-booking-predicate OR (personal-booking-predicate AND startTime >= from). Every team booking for an authorized team is included even when it fails the date range or any other AND predicate the caller adds. The event-type filter has the same shape, `("eventTypeId" = id) OR ("eventParentId" = id)`, with no outer parentheses. Interpolating it as `WHERE ${auth} AND ${eventTypeFilter}` is parsed as (auth AND eventTypeId = id) OR (eventParentId = id), so any booking whose parent event type matches is returned even if authorization fails. getBaseConditions does wrap both sides when a filter is present, but the no-filter return value and the public getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions fragments are not embed-safe. The old Prisma where-objects were grouped by the query engine, so this is a regression of the raw-SQL conversion. Wrap every fragment in an outer pair of parentheses before returning it.

Prisma.sql toEqual checks do not match nested fragments

The team-scope assertion here, the org-scope assertion around line 332, and the combined-filter assertion around line 429 expect a single flat Prisma.sql template via toEqual. The service builds those conditions with Array.reduce, nesting Prisma.sql fragments, and Prisma.sql does not flatten nested fragments until execution. The actual object has inner Sql values; the expected object has raw ids and arrays in values. Deep equality fails even when the SQL text and parameters match, so these tests fail in CI and do not validate authorization or filter SQL. Compare a flattened statement and parameter list, or execute the SQL.

Team and org authorization SQL is never executed

The only database query in this file is the user-scope getBaseConditions case, which is userId equality AND teamId IS NULL. Team and org authorization, including teamId/userId = ANY(array) and the isTeamBooking OR groups, are only compared as objects. PostgreSQL array binding for Prisma raw parameters and AND/OR precedence are therefore untested. Execute those fragments with $queryRaw against rows that must be included and rows that must be excluded (another org's team, a non-member personal booking, a team booking versus a personal booking, and an extra AND predicate such as a date range).

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Empty updateMany throws after cache is written

fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now ends with SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}). Prisma Client rejects an empty updateMany data object (Argument data must not be empty) with PrismaClientValidationError, so the method throws after CalendarCache rows have already been upserted. unwatchCalendar in this same class awaits that call after it has already stopped Google watches, cleared channel fields, and deleted cache, so unwatch now fails even though the remaining calendars' cache was rewritten. Webhook-driven refresh uses this method too; a non-2xx response makes Google retry, re-query the Calendar API, and hit the same throw on every notification. An empty update would also not bump @updatedAt even if it were accepted, so the comment's intent is not met. This PR's UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt, not SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, so the call looks unnecessary. Remove it, or if a touch is required pass { updatedAt: new Date() }. The new helper also types data as Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput, which is not the UpdateManyMutationInput updateMany accepts, so the helper can fail typecheck as well.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Webhook script writes the wrong env file and breaks on Linux

ENV_FILE is ../.env relative to the process cwd, not the script directory. bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repo root therefore creates or edits a .env outside the repository and never sets GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL for the app, then prints success. The edit on line 68 uses sed -i '', which is BSD/macOS-only; GNU sed treats '' as the script and fails the substitution. set -e is off, and cleanup always exits 0, so a missing tunnel URL, the Tunnelmole rate limit, and a failed sed all look successful. Resolve the env path from the script directory and use a portable in-place edit.

true_positives.golden_comment: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cache timestamp is always formatted en-US

The only user-visible cache status value is formatted with new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" }). The component already calls useLocale(), but the timestamp ignores the active locale and the user's 12/24-hour time format, so every non-US user sees a US short date and a 12-hour clock in Last updated. Format with the current i18n locale and the user's time format instead of a hardcoded en-US formatter.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.

false_positives.candidate:
Cache delete authorization has no tests

deleteCacheHandler is a new mutation whose only authorization is credential.findFirst({ id: credentialId, userId: user.id }) before calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } }). This PR adds no tests. Dropping or widening that filter would let any logged-in user wipe another user's calendar cache by credential id, and nothing checks that a non-owner is rejected, that only that credential's rows are removed, or that connectedCalendars actually attaches cacheUpdatedAt from getCacheStatusByCredentialIds. Add allow and deny handler tests before shipping the endpoint.

Cache delete never refreshes connected calendars

deleteCache.useMutation only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. The disconnect mutation in the same component invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and viewer.apps.integrations in onSettled; delete does not. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper owns the connectedCalendars query and passes its optional onChanged through as onSuccess, without refetching that query. After a successful delete the menu still shows the previous cacheUpdatedAt and the Delete cached data action, so the UI contradicts the success toast. Delete also only runs calendarCache.deleteMany and leaves Google watch channels active, so a later webhook can insert a new row before the user reloads. Invalidate connectedCalendars in onSettled the same way disconnect does.

Existing cache rows all get the migration timestamp

updatedAt is added as NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), so every existing CalendarCache row is stamped with the migration time instead of the last real cache write. getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns MAX(updatedAt) and the new menu shows it as Last updated. Right after deploy, every Google credential with any cache row looks freshly synced, including expired rows, because the status query does not filter expiresAt. That makes the status feature wrong for all current data until the next upsert. The header comment is also false: it says a required column without a default cannot be added to a non-empty table, but the SQL does set a default, which can make an operator abort a production migrate. Backfill from a real proxy (expiresAt minus the 30-day CACHING_TIME used when writing the cache) and correct the comment. NOW() is not a constant default, so PostgreSQL must rewrite CalendarCache under AccessExclusiveLock rather than using the instant add-column path, which blocks cache reads and writes for the length of the rewrite.

UserWithCalendars requires fields this function never reads

UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId on allSelectedCalendars and userLevelSelectedCalendars, but getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb never reads either field. The function is exported, including the legacy getConnectedDestinationCalendars alias documented for @calcom/platform-libraries, so callers that previously passed selected calendars with only externalId, integration, and eventTypeId no longer typecheck. The only caller updated here is UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession, which now selects googleChannelId (the internal Google push-channel id) into the session user on every authenticated load just to satisfy the wider Pick. Drop the new required fields and the session select unless something in this change actually consumes them.

dev:cron switched to undeclared tsx via npx

dev:cron changed from ts-node cron-tester.ts to npx tsx cron-tester.ts. ts-node is a declared devDependency of @calcom/web; tsx is not. Under Yarn Berry, npx can skip the workspace install, prompt to download an arbitrary latest tsx, or fail non-interactively. This unrelated change regresses yarn dev:cron. Revert it, or add tsx as a dependency and run it through Yarn.

true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reminder cancellation is never awaited, so the cancelled flag can be dropped

deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are fired inside forEach and never awaited, then the handler awaits unrelated deletes and returns "Booking successfully cancelled." The email fix only persists if WorkflowReminder.cancelled is updated, and SMS cancellation only happens inside that discarded promise. The same un-awaited pattern is in handleNewBooking.ts around line 966, packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx around line 488, and packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx around lines 212, 376, 519, and 574. On serverless the isolate can freeze when the response is sent, so the update never commits and the reminder is still delivered. The try/catch around the reschedule forEach does not help: forEach does not await, and both helpers swallow their own errors. This replaces an awaited prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany. Callers must await every cancellation (Promise.all or for-of) before returning or deleting parent rows.

true_positives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
immediateDelete reintroduces the SendGrid 100-cap and drops the retry record

When immediateDelete is true the helper POSTs a SendGrid batch cancel and returns without setting cancelled and without deleting the WorkflowReminder. Callers pass true for reschedules (handleNewBooking.ts:968) and for workflow/step deletion (workflows.tsx:214 and workflows.tsx:521). That immediate POST is the usage this PR is trying to stop: cancelled batches stay in SendGrid scheduled_sends until the original send time, and the cap is 100 pending cancellations. Reschedules and workflow deletes fill that cap, later cancels fail, and those emails are still sent. Failures are caught inside the helper, so the caller continues as if cancellation worked. On reschedule the booking is kept, the row is left with cancelled unset, and the cron only cancels cancelled=true rows, so it will not retry. On workflow and step deletion the POST is not awaited and the following delete cascade-removes the reminder (WorkflowStep/Workflow onDelete: Cascade). If the POST has not finished or failed because of the cap, the batch id is gone and the cron cannot retry, so the email is sent. Far-future sends should only set cancelled and keep the row. A workflow or step must not cascade the reminder away until SendGrid cancel has succeeded.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

false_positives.candidate:
All email cancels are deferred, so reminders due before the next cron are still sent

For any reminder that already has a referenceId, cancellation only sets cancelled=true and never calls SendGrid, no matter how soon scheduledDate is. The only follow-up is the scheduleEmailReminders cron (PR: every 15 minutes), which cancels batches whose scheduledDate is within the next hour. SendGrid will not cancel a scheduled send less than 10 minutes before sendAt. If the booking is cancelled after the last cron run that is still more than 10 minutes before send time, the next run either happens after scheduledDate — and that job first deletes every EMAIL reminder with scheduledDate <= now, so cancel is never attempted — or SendGrid rejects the late cancel. The reminder is delivered. This is the common case of cancelling shortly before a reminder. Deferral also does not protect the 100-cap for sends already inside the one-hour window, because those cancellations would be pending for under an hour either way. Reminders already inside that window should be cancelled immediately; only later sends should be flagged for the cron.

Every workflow save recreates reminders while old SendGrid batches stay live

An existing step is treated as edited when JSON.stringify(oldStep) !== JSON.stringify(newStep). oldStep is a Prisma WorkflowStep and always includes numberVerificationPending; newStep is the zod input and has senderName instead, so the comparison is always true even when nothing changed. The branch used to delete the WorkflowReminder row; that deleteMany was removed. It now only calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder (line 576), which sets cancelled and leaves the SendGrid scheduled send in place, and that call is not awaited. The same request then scheduleEmailReminder's a new batch for every future booking of that step. Every workflow save therefore leaves the previous batches live until the cron's one-hour window and adds another set. Near-term reminders can be delivered twice. All superseded batches become pending cancellations in the same hour, which can exceed SendGrid's 100-cap and cause the cron cancel loop to fail. Compare the actual editable fields, and do not create the replacement send until the previous batch is flagged or cancelled.

No tests for deferred cancel or the cron SendGrid cancellation loop

The PR replaces SendGrid cancellation and adds a cron path, but no test covers deleteScheduledEmailReminder, the cancelled flag, reschedule/workflow-delete behavior, or the scheduleEmailReminders cancellation loop. The previous fix used the wrong SendGrid endpoint and failed in production once 100 pending cancellations accumulated. Without a test that a far-future cancel only sets cancelled, that an imminent cancel actually stops the batch, and that one failed POST does not skip the remaining rows, the same production failure can regress unnoticed.

One SendGrid cancel failure aborts the rest and skips DB cleanup

remindersToCancel is handled in a single try/catch. Each POST is awaited in order, and the prisma deletes are only executed after every request succeeds. Any rejection — the 100 pending-cancellation cap, SendGrid refusing a cancel inside its 10-minute cutoff, a null referenceId, or a network error — jumps to the catch, which only logs, then the handler goes on to schedule new mail. Later reminders in that run are not cancelled. Rows whose POST already succeeded are not deleted, so the next run must redo them. A row that fails every time stays in the result set until its scheduledDate passes and the earlier deleteMany removes it, and each run that hits it aborts the rest of the batch, so those other cancelled reminders are sent. The query also does not require method EMAIL or a non-null referenceId, so one bad row is enough to fail the POST. Handle each reminder independently, skip rows without a batch id, and delete a row only after its own cancel succeeds.

Paid booking cancellation returns before workflow reminders are cancelled

If the booking is paid, this branch refunds, sets status to REJECTED, and returns "Booking successfully cancelled." before the reminder block at line 484. That block is the only place this handler marks email reminders cancelled or deletes SMS reminders. The earlier return null when the payment app is missing (around line 437) skips it too. Paid event types can still have workflows, and bookingToDelete already loads workflowReminders, but they are ignored on this path. A cancelled paid booking therefore keeps its scheduled emails and SMS. If the reminder was not yet handed to SendGrid, the cron's unscheduled query does not check booking status and will schedule and send it; if it was already scheduled, the cron only cancels rows with cancelled=true, which was never set. Reminder cancellation has to run on this path before returning.

Past-due reminders are deleted before SendGrid cancellation is attempted

The cron starts by deleting every EMAIL WorkflowReminder with scheduledDate <= now, including rows with cancelled=true, and only then loads reminders to cancel (lines 44-51). The row is the only copy of the SendGrid batch id. If an earlier run did not cancel that batch (downtime, a thrown cancel aborting the loop, or the booking being cancelled after the last pre-send run), SendGrid still has the scheduled mail and this delete makes a later cancel impossible. Past-due cleanup must not remove cancelled rows until a SendGrid cancel has been attempted and the outcome recorded. As written, any missed window permanently fails the fix.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reschedule cleanup uses forEach(async) and never finishes

In packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts the calendar/video cleanup at line 125 was switched to bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) so it can await the now-async getCalendar. Array.forEach does not wait for async callbacks and drops their return values, so the try/catch around it never sees failures, and Reschedule still sends the reschedule email and returns true while deletion is in flight. This is a regression from the async app-store change: previously getCalendar was synchronous, so deleteEvent was at least invoked before the callback yielded, and deleteMeeting started the provider call before returning. Now the calendar path awaits getCalendar before deleteEvent, and deleteMeeting (videoClient.ts) awaits getVideoAdapters before calling the provider, and nothing awaits either promise. The old event can remain on the external calendar and the video meeting can stay up; on serverless the runtime often freezes that work after the handler returns, so the cleanup never runs. Replace forEach with for...of or Promise.all and await both getCalendar/deleteEvent and deleteMeeting inside the try.

true_positives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Top-level import() preloads every app and can crash on a failed one
