Enter in the group form activates Add instead of Save

The new form wraps the name field, the user selector, and the action buttons, but none of the buttons set type="button" and the form has no submit handler. In HTML the default button type is submit, and pressing Enter in a text field synthetically clicks the first submit button in the form. Once the group has an id, that button is Add, not Save. Enter in the name field therefore runs addMembers (re-adding whatever is still in the username box) and does not save the name, visibility, or alias level. If Ember's action helper does not preventDefault, the form also does a GET navigation of the current admin URL and discards the in-page state. On a new group the first button is Save, so Enter behaves differently before and after the first save.

Add and remove failures are silent and the username field is never cleared

addMembers posts the usernames and, on success, does not clear the field (the TODO on the previous line). removeMember and addMembers both ignore rejected promises. A 422 (automatic group), 404 (member already gone), 500 (duplicate add), or network error closes the confirm dialog or clicks Add and then changes nothing on screen, so the admin cannot tell failure from a no-op. Because the field stays filled, a second click resubmits the same names; if Group#add raises on a duplicate, that second click 500s. Newly added users are also only reloaded on the current offset, so someone who sorts onto another page never appears in the list even though the request succeeded.

Username box is not reset when switching groups

Admin group controllers are Ember singletons. setupController replaces the model and reloads members but does not clear controller.usernames. The add-members field is bound to that controller property, and addMembers never clears it after a successful add either. Navigating from group A to group B leaves A's pending (or just-added) usernames in the box; clicking Add then PUTs those names onto group B. Offset is stored on the group model so it does not leak, but usernames were left on the shared controller when membership was split out of the save payload.

Member reloads use the unsaved name from the text field

findMembers builds GET /groups/<name>/members.json from this.get('name'), and the admin name input is two-way bound to that property. Editing the name and then paging, adding, or removing a member fetches (or fails to fetch) the unsaved name before Save. Remove itself uses the numeric id and can succeed, but the follow-up findMembers 404s, so the list never refreshes and the removed user stays on screen. The name is also interpolated without encodeURIComponent, so a value that still contains spaces produces a broken URL. Pagination has already written the new offset before the request, so a failed reload leaves the page indicator and the member list out of sync.

Client keeps the unstripped name after create

create() only copies resp.basic_group.id from the POST response. The server strips the name before save and returns the stored name on BasicGroupSerializer, but the in-memory group keeps whatever was typed, including leading or trailing spaces. showGroup then navigates with that unsaved name, so a refresh looks the group up by the spaced name, misses the record named "bob", and the admin route sends the user back to the index. A later Save sends the spaced name to update, which assigns params[:name] with no strip (create strips, update does not). That either fails name-format validation or writes the spaces back over the cleaned name.

GET group members no longer returns a bare array

GroupsController#members used to render_serialized an array of GroupUserSerializer objects. It now returns {members, meta: {total, limit, offset}}. The in-repo Group.findMembers client was updated, but any other caller — plugins, API scripts, or a browser still running the previous JS that did result.map(...) — will throw because the top-level JSON is an object. The reverse is also true during a rolling deploy: new JS expects result.members and result.meta and crashes on the old array. There is no versioned path or compatibility shim, and no spec locks the new contract.

Overlapping member-page requests can land on the wrong page

next and previous write offset and call findMembers immediately, and the pager links are not disabled while a request is in flight. Two quick clicks start two GETs; findMembers applies whichever response arrives last via setProperties, including that response's offset. A slower response for the previous page overwrites a later click, so the list and the page indicator show a page the admin already left. Nothing ignores a stale response.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
should_block? writes during validation and double-counts

should_block? is not a pure predicate: on every hit it does match_count += 1, sets last_match_at, and calls record.save, and EmailValidator calls it from User validation. UsersController#create always evaluates user.valid? and then user.save, and save runs validations again, so one signup attempt invokes should_block? twice. The first save commits immediately. The second runs inside the user-save transaction: if the user is persisted (including action_type do_nothing, which still updates stats), both increments commit and match_count rises by 2; if validation fails, the inner increment rolls back and the count rises by 1. Paths that only save once, such as User.create_for_email, rise by 1. Any valid? call, including a check that never creates a user, also mutates the row. The read-modify-write is racy under concurrent signups, and a failure in that save (lock timeout, StatementInvalid) escapes the validator and is rescued in create as login.something_already_taken. Record the match with one atomic UPDATE that does not run validations, and do not write from inside validation on every valid?/save pass.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same underlying issue: a blocking predicate mutates statistics during a read/validation check, making it impure and creating concurrency risks. Its additional discussion of double-counting and validation paths elaborates on those side effects.

true_positives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Domain allow/deny regex is unanchored and can be bypassed

email_in_restriction_setting? builds Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true) after only escaping dots, then uses value =~ regexp, which succeeds on any substring. With email_domains_whitelist set to example.com, attacker@example.com.evil.com matches @example.com and is treated as allowed. Someone who controls that domain can receive the activation message and register even though the address is not on example.com. The same pattern does not cover subdomains on the blacklist: spam.com does not match user@mail.spam.com, so a subdomain of a blocked provider is accepted. Other metacharacters in the site setting are interpolated raw, so a value with an unmatched parenthesis makes Regexp.new raise and turns every email change into a 500. Compare normalized domains (anchor at the end of the address, or split the setting and test equality) instead of a substring regex.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same unanchored domain regex in email_in_restriction_setting? that permits whitelist bypass through partial domain matching. The candidate gives a different exploit example and additional concerns, but explicitly identifies the underlying boundary-anchoring flaw.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocklist lookup is case-sensitive and does not trim

BlockedEmail.should_block? loads a row with BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first, and the model never normalizes email before the uniqueness check or save. Signup stores the address exactly as submitted (User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] with no downcase or strip), and the new client cache compares that same raw string via rejectedEmails.contains. On PostgreSQL the unique index and equality match are case-sensitive, so a block row for bad@spam.com does not match Bad@spam.com, BAD@spam.com, or bad@spam.com with leading or trailing whitespace. Those are the same mailbox in practice (UsersController#change_email already does Email.downcase(...).strip), so a blocked address can still register by changing case or padding spaces, and after one rejection the signup form will allow that variant through again. Downcase and strip on write and inside should_block? before the query, and enforce case-insensitive uniqueness so mixed-case duplicates cannot be stored.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same case-sensitive email lookup in BlockedEmail.should_block? and explains how changing email capitalization bypasses a block. Its additional whitespace and normalization concerns do not change the core match.

false_positives.candidate:
Email change never consults the blocklist

The new block check only runs from EmailValidator when a User is validated with email_changed?. UsersController#change_email never assigns user.email or saves the user. It only rejects the address if User.where("email = ?", lower_email).exists?, then creates an EmailToken and enqueues an authorization mail to that address. A blocked address therefore passes this endpoint and a confirmation message is sent. Whether the address actually sticks depends on EmailToken.confirm later performing a validating save; this request path itself does not enforce BlockedEmail.should_block?, so the control added for signup is missing on the email-change flow. Reject blocked addresses here before creating the token, using the same normalization as lower_email.

rejectedEmails array is shared across controller instances

rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) is evaluated once when CreateAccountController is defined, so the array sits on the prototype. pushObject mutates that array in place rather than assigning a per-instance property. Every instance then shares one list: a second controller (tests, App.reset(), or another create()) already contains emails rejected elsewhere and will fail emailValidation for them via contains. Set a fresh array in init with this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A()) so instances do not leak rejections into each other.

Validator specs stub the block check and miss bypasses

The EmailValidator examples stub BlockedEmail.should_block? and never insert a BlockedEmail, so they cannot catch a case or whitespace mismatch, a failed lookup, or the write inside should_block?. blocked_email_spec.rb only uses the exact address block@spamfromhome.org and calls should_block? once, so it stays green if Bad@spam.com or a trailing space is allowed, and if UsersController#create increments match_count twice. Domain whitelist and blacklist behavior was moved into EmailValidator with no regression example, including the unanchored match of attacker@example.com.evil.com against a whitelist of example.com. Add cases for normalized lookup, a single stat update on the signup path, and anchored domain restrictions.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
align-items() mixin emits invalid and unmapped legacy values

@mixin align-items forwards $alignment unchanged to -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align, and also emits -ms-align-items, which is not a real property (IE10/11 only implement -ms-flex-align). The 2009/2012 properties accept start and end, not flex-start and flex-end. @include align-items(flex-start) therefore produces a working unprefixed align-items: flex-start and legacy declarations those engines drop as invalid, so items fall back to the default stretch in the browsers this mixin is meant to cover. center and baseline, the only current call sites, happen to be valid in both syntaxes, so header and badge alignment are not broken by this today. Map flex-start to start and flex-end to end on the legacy properties only, and delete the -ms-align-items line.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies -ms-align-items as nonexistent, names -ms-flex-align as the correct legacy property, and recommends deleting the invalid declaration. Its additional value-mapping concern does not change this direct match.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order() mixin applies 0-based values to 1-based box-ordinal-group

@mixin order copies $val unchanged into -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group. Those 2009 properties are 1-based and default to 1; modern order, -ms-flex-order, and -webkit-order are 0-based and default to 0. Legacy declarations must be $val + 1 (what Autoprefixer and Bourbon emit). As written, order(0) becomes ordinal-group 0 (invalid or sorted before every default item) and order(1) ties the item with every sibling that does not set an ordinal, whose default is already 1, so those items tie or swap in old WebKit/Firefox box layout while modern browsers keep the intended order. The current call sites pass 2 and 3, which still sort after the legacy default of 1, so this header does not mis-order today, but this mixin is the shared helper the PR adds and the first use of the normal values 0 or 1 will disagree across the browsers the prefixes exist for.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same indexing bug: the mixin passes $val unchanged to legacy -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group properties, which require 1-based values, causing incorrect legacy-browser ordering when $val is 0.

false_positives.candidate:
Small-action flex conversion leaves action buttons off the right edge

.small-action is now a flex row, but the old full-width float layout was removed without a flex replacement. Direct children are flex items, so float on them is ignored, and .small-action-desc stays at the initial flex: 0 1 auto (no flex-grow / flex: 1), so it shrink-wraps to its text instead of stretching across the row. The previous padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em, which made that block full width and kept text clear of the floated 45px avatar, was replaced with padding: 0 1.5%. The action button is still only float: right (line 309). If the button is a flex item, that float is ignored and there is no margin-left: auto, so it sits in source order next to the text. If it is nested in the description, the float still applies but only to the content-sized description box, not the post row. Either way undelete/delete/edit controls that used to pin to the right edge of the small-action row now sit immediately after short action text ("closed", "deleted", and similar). Browsers that ignore the new display values still honor float: left on .topic-avatar, and with the 4em offset gone the description overlaps the icon.

Header panel is not pinned right under the legacy flex display values

.panel lost float: right and is now pinned with margin-left: auto, while .d-header .contents is turned into a flex container by the new flexbox() mixin (and .title { float: left } was removed). Auto margins absorb free space only in modern flexbox. The mixin also emits display: -webkit-box and display: -ms-flexbox before display: flex, and those are the values IE10 and old WebKit actually keep, because they do not understand display: flex. In the 2009 box model and in IE10's 2012 flexbox, margin-left: auto does not consume free space, and float does not apply to flex/box items, so the removed float is not a fallback. Login, signup, notification, and user-menu controls therefore stay in source order immediately after the logo (and topic title) instead of at the right edge of the header — the browsers those prefixes were added to support. Pin the panel with a growing sibling (-webkit-box-flex: 1 and -ms-flex: 1) or the prefixed pack/justify properties, not auto margin alone.

Header extra-info flex item can push controls off-screen

order: 2 on .extra-info-wrapper only works if that element is a flex item of .d-header .contents, which is the new flex container, alongside .panel at order 3. As a flex item it keeps the default min-width: auto, so it will not shrink below its content's minimum size, and this change never sets min-width: 0, overflow: hidden, or flex: 1. .panel's margin-left: auto only moves the controls to the right when free space remains after items are sized. A long topic title (min-content is the longest unbreakable word, or the whole title if it cannot wrap) plus the logo and the icon panel overflows the header; the auto margin collapses to zero and the notification/user controls are pushed past the viewport or the page scrolls horizontally. Docked-header titles need min-width: 0 and ellipsis, or the row cannot shrink.

Header category bullet loses its vertical alignment offset

The nested &.bullet { margin-top: 5px } rule under .extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper was removed, and nothing replaces that offset. align-items: center on .d-header .contents only centers the whole extra-info wrapper against the logo and icons. The category bullet is still a float: left child of the wrapper (line 34), so its position relative to the topic title text is independent of the parent's flex alignment. line-height: 1.5 on the wrapper does not restore a 5px shift of the floated badge. The bullet in the docked header topic strip will sit about 5px higher than before relative to the title text.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is never used as the serializer include hook

ActiveModel Serializers emits an attribute unless include_<attribute>? exists and returns false. This method is named include_website_name without the question mark, so it is never called and the website.present? guard is dead. Every UserSerializer payload therefore includes website_name, with null when the website is blank, unlike location and website which are omitted when blank. Renaming this method to include_website_name? without removing it would also override the include_website_name? defined earlier by untrusted_attributes, because the class-body method is defined later, and that would drop the anonymous TL0 check.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same missing '?' suffix on include_website_name and its effect on conditional attribute inclusion. It does not mention the string-literal mutation concern, but it directly matches the golden comment's primary issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Same-site check shows paths for unrelated hosts and hides them for www

website_name appends URI#path only when it decides the website host is the same site as Discourse.current_hostname, but the comparison is incorrect. The branch at line 144 treats two hosts as the same whenever they have an equal label count greater than 2 and share every label after the first. For a forum at forum.co.uk, forum.com.au, name.github.io, or app.herokuapp.com that matches every other host under that public suffix, so http://unrelated.co.uk/secret is rendered as unrelated.co.uk/secret instead of unrelated.co.uk. The else branch only appends the path when the forum hostname string-ends with "." plus the website host, and the exact-match branch is case-sensitive while URI#host is lowercased. A forum hostname of Example.com with website http://example.com/user therefore fails every branch and the path is dropped. The usual www/apex pair also fails: forum example.com and website http://www.example.com/user displays www.example.com with no path, which is the case this change is supposed to improve. Profiles will expose paths of unrelated sites and still hide paths for the same site.

Profile link text stays stale after the website is edited

The visible label used to be a controller computed property of model.website (host taken with split, invalidated when website changed). The template now prints the server snapshot model.website_name while href stays bound to model.website. User#save sends the edited website but only copies bio_excerpt back from the PUT response, so the in-memory website_name is left unchanged. Preferences edit that same user model, and the profile reads it without another fetch, so after a website change the anchor text can still show the previous host and path while the link points at the new URL until a full reload.

Specs never assert website_name is hidden or domain-safe

The TL0 anonymous example still only expects bio_raw, bio_cooked, bio_excerpt, location, website, profile_background, and card_background to be absent, so it stays green when website_name leaks. The new website_name examples only stub discourse.org, example.com, and forums.example.com against http://example.com/user. They never cover a public-suffix collision such as forum.co.uk versus http://other.co.uk/secret, or example.com versus http://www.example.com/user, which are the cases the matcher gets wrong. The added tests do not catch the bugs in this change.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Resize listener treats any prefix of the forum URL as a trusted origin

The check is `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, i.e. whether the forum URL string contains the sender origin, not whether the sender equals the forum origin. Any origin that is a string prefix of `discourseUrl` is accepted. For a forum at `https://discuss.example.com`, an attacker origin of `https://discuss.example.co` matches because `"https://discuss.example.com".indexOf("https://discuss.example.co") === 0`. That window can set `iframe.height` to an arbitrary value. Combined with `scrolling="no"`, a huge height covers the embedding page with the iframe. The listener also does not require `e.source === iframe.contentWindow`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify bypassable origin validation caused by using indexOf substring matching instead of exact origin comparison. Although their malicious-domain examples differ, they describe the same underlying security issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Resize postMessage never arrives in the parent

`parent.postMessage(..., request.referer)` passes the full referer URL (scheme, host, path, and query) as `targetOrigin`. Browsers of this era compare that argument to the parent's origin (`https://host`), not to the full page URL, and drop the message when they differ. `<%= request.referer %>` is also HTML-escaped, so a referer containing `&` is inserted as `&` and cannot match even in browsers that parse `targetOrigin` as a URL. `embed.js` creates the iframe with `scrolling="no"` and no height, and only grows it on `discourse-resize`. The message is discarded, so the iframe stays at the default ~150px and comments are clipped with no scrollbar.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: passing the full referrer URL rather than its origin as postMessage's targetOrigin causes the resize message to be dropped, preventing iframe resizing.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Imported HTML is stored raw and executed on the Discourse origin

RSS items and remotely fetched pages are saved with `cook_method: raw_html` and `skip_validations: true`. `Post#cook` then returns `raw` unchanged, and both the embed view (`raw post.cooked`) and the normal topic UI render `cooked` as HTML. Nothing runs the content through Sanitize. `ruby-readability` 0.5.7 does not honor the `tags:` / `attributes:` arguments passed in `import_remote` (those are Sanitize-style options and are ignored), so scripts, event handlers, and `javascript:` links from the remote page are kept. `PollFeed` also `CGI.unescapeHTML`s the feed body first, turning entity-encoded markup into live tags. Separately, line 13 interpolates the source URL into a single-quoted `href` and into the link text with no encoding; `absolutize_urls` reparses with Nokogiri, which preserves injected elements and handlers. A feed link or embed URL such as `http://example.com/' onclick='alert(1)` becomes an active handler in the stored post. A normal CMS feed that includes an embed script is enough; the script runs as the viewing user on the forum origin, including inside the embed iframe.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies the XSS caused by unescaped source URL interpolation in TopicEmbed.import's generated HTML, matching the golden comment's security issue. It does not mention the separate NoMethodError when contents is nil.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Embed highlights template is invalid Ruby and 500s

`<%- end if %>` is compiled as Ruby `end if`, which is a syntax error (a block `if` is closed with `end`, not `end if`). ERB turns the whole template into one method, so any render of `embed/best` raises SyntaxError before HTML is produced. The first visit can still show `loading.html.erb` and enqueue a retrieve; once a `topic_embeds` row exists, every later iframe load 500s and the discussion never appears. The new controller spec does not enable `render_views`, so it never compiles this template and stays green.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same invalid ERB closing syntax, `end if`, which causes a Ruby syntax error during rendering and should be replaced with `end`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed polling crashes on ordinary RSS items

`i.content.scrub` assumes every item has a string `content` and that `String#scrub` exists. Standard RSS 2.0 only has `description` (SimpleRSS sets `content` from `content:encoded`), so `i.content` is nil and this raises NoMethodError on the first such item. `String#scrub` itself was added in Ruby 2.1, so on Ruby 2.0/1.9 the call fails even when content is present. There is no per-item rescue, and `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so one bad item aborts the rest of the feed until the next hour. `TopicRetriever` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute` inline before the HTTP fallback, so the same exception also skips `import_remote` for the URL the user actually asked to embed. `feed_key` is computed and never used, and `open` is not given a timeout or closed.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies that RSS items may lack content, causing i.content.scrub to raise when content is nil, and notes that standard RSS uses description. This matches the golden issue despite additional unrelated concerns.

false_positives.candidate:
import_remote fetches the embed URL with open-uri and follows redirects

`import_remote` does `open(url).read` with no `require 'open-uri'` in this file (only `poll_feed.rb` requires it), no read size limit, no timeout, and no close. Unless some other file has already loaded open-uri, `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a local path and raises Errno::ENOENT, so the non-RSS embed path never imports. When open-uri is loaded, it follows HTTP redirects. `TopicRetriever` only compares the original URL's host to `embeddable_host`, so `http://allowed-host/redirect` that 302s to `http://127.0.0.1`, link-local cloud metadata, or another internal service is fetched and then stored as a public topic via the raw_html path. The embed action enqueues that fetch for any client that can set `Referer` to the allowed host. The same method is also called from the Disqus importer with links taken from the XML, with no host allowlist. Failures are unrescued, so a 404, SSL error, or huge body fails the job.

embed_url is varchar(255) under a unique index

`t.string :embed_url` is a varchar(255) on PostgreSQL, and the unique index is on that column. Article URLs with long slugs or tracking query strings routinely exceed 255 characters. `TopicEmbed.create!` then raises a string-right-truncation error, the import transaction rolls back, and that article can never be embedded. The column needs to be `text` (or a much larger limit); a unique btree index on text is valid in PostgreSQL.

Disqus import drops threads when the live page cannot be fetched

Topic creation used to be a local `PostCreator` call with the export title, `created_at`, permalink body, and optional `-c` category. It now depends entirely on `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which GETs `t[:link]` and returns nil on any network, HTTP, or readability failure. The comment loop is inside `if post.present?`, so a dead or blocked link silently skips every comment on that thread. `import_remote` / `TopicEmbed.import` also have no `created_at` or category argument, and the `-c` / `--category` option was removed, so existing invocations that passed a category fail and imported topics are dated now in the default category instead of the original thread date and destination.

Bulk embed imports still hit create rate limiters

`skip_validations: true` only turns off ActiveRecord validations. `Post` still includes `RateLimiter::OnCreateRecord` (`rate_limit` / `rate_limit_create_post`, plus topic creation limits in `TopicCreator`), and those callbacks run on save. A feed or retrieve that creates more than a handful of topics in one run will raise `RateLimiter::LimitExceeded` or roll back mid-loop; `PollFeed` has no per-item rescue, so the rest of the feed is skipped until the limit window resets (`max_topics_per_day` is 20). The Disqus task in this same change calls `RateLimiter.disable` around its import loop; `PollFeed` and `TopicRetriever` do not. Updates pass `bypass_rate_limiter`, but that flag only skips `EditRateLimiter` inside `PostRevisor`, not create limits.

Every embed miss re-downloads and imports the entire feed

When `feed_polling_enabled?` is set, each cache miss calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute` synchronously inside the retrieve job, before the single-URL HTTP fetch. The Redis throttle key is per embed URL, not per feed, so ten different articles trigger ten full feed downloads and imports per minute, on top of the hourly schedule (this path does not take the scheduler lock, so it can overlap the hourly run). `PollFeed#feed_key` looks like a conditional-GET / already-seen short-circuit but is never read, and `poll_feed` always `open`s the feed URL and walks every item. One slow or huge feed blocks the worker and can create a topic for every item as a side effect of viewing a single embed.

Retrieve throttle can stick forever if expire does not run

`retrieved_recently?` does `SETNX retrieved:<url> 1` and only then `EXPIRE 60`. Those are not atomic. If the process dies, Redis errors, or expire is skipped between the two calls, the key has no TTL. `retrieved_recently?` then stays true for that exact URL forever (unless `no_throttle` is set for staff), so the article is never fetched again. Use a single `SET key 1 NX EX 60` (or set the TTL inside the same command the deployment's Redis supports). The same gap exists for every distinct embed URL.

Embed URLs are compared exactly, so the same article splits or is skipped

Lookup, uniqueness, and the import short-circuit all use the raw URL string (`where(embed_url: url)` and the unique index). There is no normalization: `http://host/a` and `http://host/a/`, a URL with a fragment or `utm_*` query, and the same path with a different scheme case are different rows, so one article becomes multiple topics. The allowlist check is also case-sensitive: `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` uses `URI(embed_url).host`, which preserves case (`Example.COM`), and compares it to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` with `!=`. `TopicEmbed.import` only accepts URLs matching `/^https?:\/\//`, so `HTTP://...` is dropped. `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` uses the same case-sensitive host compare on `Referer`. Mixed-case canonical URLs from a CMS or feed never import, and the loading iframe retries forever.

Deleting the topic or first post leaves a row that crashes embed and feed updates

`belongs_to :topic` / `:post` do not declare `dependent: :destroy`, and `Topic` is not given a matching association, so destroying a topic or its first post leaves `topic_embeds` in place (there is also no foreign key). The embed action then does `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` for a missing topic and 500s on every view instead of importing again. On the next feed change, `post = embed.post` is nil and `PostRevisor.new(post)` raises, which aborts the rest of `PollFeed`'s item loop. `import` also treats any in-memory `PostCreator` result as success (`post.present?` is true for an unsaved post after a rolled-back create) and will `create!` an embed pointing at a topic id that was never committed.

Anyone who can set Referer can enqueue unbounded outbound fetches

`ensure_embeddable` only compares `Referer`'s host to `embeddable_host`. That header is not a credential; any client can send `Referer: http://<embeddable_host>/` and GET `/embed/best?embed_url=...`. On a cache miss the action always `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic)` with the caller-supplied URL and no per-IP or global limit. The job's 60s Redis throttle is per exact URL, so many distinct paths on the allowed host become many Sidekiq jobs and many outbound requests (and, after redirects, internal ones). `loading.html.erb` reloads every 30 seconds and enqueues again. `TopicRetriever` returns quietly on host mismatch, blank `embed_by_username`, throttle, or fetch failure, but the UI has no error state, so a misconfiguration or attacker page keeps scheduling work forever. This is a GET that mutates server state (jobs and topics), so crawlers and prefetch can trigger it too when a matching referer is present.

absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs and skips other relative ones

The helper claims to absolutize relative URLs but only rewrites `a[href]` and `img[src]` that `start_with?('/')`. A protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/a.png` matches that check, then `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, so it is rewritten to `http://<article-host>/cdn.example.com/a.png` instead of keeping the CDN host. Relative URLs that do not start with `/` (`images/a.png`, `../a.png`, `?page=2`) are left unchanged and later resolve against the Discourse origin, so images and links 404 or hit forum routes. Both forms are common in RSS and article HTML. Only root-relative paths like `/hello` work, which is the only case the new spec covers.

import mutates contents in place and crashes when the body is nil

`contents << footer` appends to the caller's string instead of copying it. `import_remote` passes `doc.content` through, and Readability returns nil when it cannot extract an article, so this raises NoMethodError and the retrieve job fails (the loading iframe then retries forever). A frozen string raises the same way. Callers that reuse the buffer also get a second footer and a different SHA1 on the next import. Build a new string (`"#{contents}#{footer}"`) after rejecting blank content.

Embed controller spec never renders the templates it claims succeed

The success examples do not call `render_views` (rspec-rails 2 stubs views by default), so they never compile `best.html.erb` and cannot catch the `end if` syntax error. The example that expects a topic view stubs `TopicView.new` without a return value; mocha yields nil, so `@topic_view` is nil and a real render would raise before the `after` hook's `response.should be_success`. `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only stubs whether `execute` calls `poll_feed` and never parses a feed, so the nil-`content` crash and unsanitized import are also untested.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

The Tempfile fd stays on the old inode, while tempfile.size (fstat on that fd) is what both the while condition and Upload.create_for use as the filesize. After a replace, the recorded size can be the original multi-megabyte size while the path holds the smaller image, or create_for can persist the pre-downsize bytes / a truncated file. The return value is ignored, so a failed convert is retried and the damaged file is still passed to create_for. The loop can also exit while the file is still over max_image_size_kb (five 80% passes are not guaranteed to hit the byte limit, and a no-op or failed pass does not abort), despite the comment claiming the image is reduced to the allowed size. A large GIF is therefore flattened to the first frame even when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, and ImageMagick keys the writer off the destination suffix, so an extension-less output can fail or be written in the wrong format while original_filename and content_type stay unchanged. If the path does end in .gif, downsize_instructions_animated forwards the "80%" geometry to gifsicle --resize-fit, which was built for a pixel WIDTHxHEIGHT box, so animated downsize fails instead of shrinking the file.

The new loop runs OptimizedImage.downsize up to five times whenever an image is larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. Nothing in that condition caps how large the file may be. true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing TopicUser row 500s unsubscribe

unsubscribe loads TopicUser with find_by(user_id, topic_id) and immediately reads tu.notification_level. If there is no row, tu is nil and this raises NoMethodError, so the request 500s and nothing is saved. A topic_users row is not created for every user who can see a topic; the URL is predictable and any logged-in user who can see the topic can open it without having visited or been emailed. TopicUser.change already creates the row when it is missing; this action does not use it.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same nil dereference: when no TopicUser record exists, tu is nil, and accessing tu.notification_level raises an exception.

false_positives.candidate:
Unsubscribe is a state-changing GET

TopicsController#unsubscribe is exposed as GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and t/:topic_id/unsubscribe, and it writes topic_users.notification_level before rendering. Rails CSRF protection does not cover GET, and this app predates SameSite cookies, so a logged-in victim can be forced to change topic or PM notification level by an image, link prefetch, or other cross-site GET. The write is also not idempotent: a level above regular becomes regular, and regular becomes muted, so a refresh or a second full page load applies a second transition (watching becomes regular, then muted). The Ember unsubscribe route never performs the change itself, so the only implementation of the action is this GET side effect.

Unsubscribe leaves tracking and watching users notified

The email string says the link will stop notifications for this topic, and the new page says the user will stop receiving them, but unsubscribe only sets notification_level to muted when it is already regular (1) or lower. Tracking (2) and watching (3) are both written to regular (1). Tracking receives the same reply, mention, and quote emails as regular, so that click changes nothing about email. Watching stops every-post emails but still sends reply, mention, and quote emails. A second request then takes regular to muted, so the first confirmation is false and a refresh changes the result.

Raw save does not record an explicit notification choice

unsubscribe assigns notification_level and calls save! instead of TopicUser.change. change is what sets notifications_changed_at, sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, and publishes the /topic/:id notification_level_change event. save! leaves the old reason in place. Rows created when an email is sent often have a nil reason, because TopicUser.change is called with only last_emailed_post_number. update_last_read in topic_user.rb then forces notification_level back to tracking when notifications_reason_id is null and the auto-track time threshold is met, and auto_track does the same for a nil reason. For those users the unsubscribe does not stick, and already-open clients never get the level-change event.

Unsubscribe template does not match its route

The router registers a top-level topicUnsubscribe route at /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe, and the route, controller, and view are all the topic-unsubscribe module. Ember looks up template topic-unsubscribe, i.e. templates/topic-unsubscribe. The template was added at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which is the name for a nested topic.unsubscribe route that was not registered, and there is no matching topic/unsubscribe controller. After the Rails shell boots, the transition fails with a missing template, so the confirmation text and the notification dropdown never render.

Per-topic unsubscribe link is not tied to the recipient

Topic#unsubscribe_url is only the public topic URL plus /unsubscribe, and UserNotifications puts that same link in every recipient's mail. TopicsController#unsubscribe is behind ensure_logged_in and always updates current_user, with no signed user or email token. Unlike the existing digest path email/unsubscribe/:key, a logged-out recipient opening the message from a mail client is not unsubscribed by the click. If someone else is logged in (forwarded mail or a shared browser), that account's notification level is changed instead of the recipient's.

render :show drops canonical URL on topic pages

perform_show_response is also used by TopicsController#show, which calls canonical_url only after perform_show_response returns. Previously the HTML format block did not render, so Rails deferred the template until the action finished and @canonical_url was already set for the layout. The new render :show inside format.html renders the layout immediately, before that call, so every topic HTML response loses its canonical link. Unsubscribe HTML has the same gap because it never sets a canonical URL either.

No coverage of unsubscribe behavior or the new link

The only spec change passes unsubscribe_url into Email::MessageBuilder so the new unsubscribe_link translation does not raise MissingInterpolationArgument, but the example still only checks that the user-preferences URL appears in the text body. It never asserts that the per-topic unsubscribe URL is present in the text or HTML part, or that List-Unsubscribe changed. There is no controller or request spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe, so the level transition, nil TopicUser crash, slug redirect, and session requirements are untested.

dev:cron changed from ts-node cron-tester.ts to npx tsx cron-tester.ts. ts-node is a declared devDependency of @calcom/web; tsx is not. true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working-hours recheck zeroes split schedules

The new working-hours fallback uses the same inverted find, and it runs for every fixed host whenever an override did not already return — including ordinary single-host events, because those users are marked isFixed. workingHours.find rejects the slot if any entry for that UTC weekday does not contain the slot start. Two intervals on the same day (a lunch break is the common case) therefore eliminate every slot, including times that fall inside one of the intervals, so those hosts get an empty booking page. Separately, end is computed from slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime, so a slot that starts inside the range but runs past workingHour.endTime is accepted. That shows up in round-robin, where aggregated hours can emit a slot another host can take after this host's hours have ended. A weekday present in no workingHours entry is not rejected either, so this check cannot enforce a fixed host's day off.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies that end is computed from slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime, matching the golden issue, even though it also discusses other bugs.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-day overrides are never recognized

A fully blocked date is stored as an override whose start and end are the same instant, and this function tries to treat that as unavailable for the whole day. The check is dayjs(...) === dayjs(...). Those are two different objects, so reference equality is never true, even when both instants match. The later before/after checks then only exclude slots that do not overlap that single point, leaving a bookable hole around the shifted timestamp. For a UTC−5 host blocked at 00:00, the instant is shifted to 05:00Z, and a slot that overlaps 05:00Z is reported available on a day the host marked unavailable. Compare with isSame (or the underlying timestamps) and, on a match, reject the whole day.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same bug: strict equality compares two distinct Day.js object references rather than their date values, so matching instants are not recognized. It also recommends isSame() as the fix.

false_positives.candidate:

In checkIfIsAvailable, if any date override falls on the slot's day and the slot is treated as inside that override, the function returns true immediately. That return is before the busy-interval loop, so Google Calendar conflicts and existing Cal.com bookings are never consulted. isFixed is true for every user when schedulingType is null and for every collective host, and the same helper is used for fixed and round-robin hosts, so this is not limited to the round-robin case. On any day that has a date override, the public schedule can offer times when that host is already busy, which is what the booking page presents.

The new override scan uses dateOverrides.find and treats a truthy callback as "this slot is unavailable". The callback returns true when the slot is entirely before or entirely after that one window, and find stops at the first such window. A normal split override (for example 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 on the same date) therefore rejects every slot, because every slot lies outside at least one window, and the day shows no availability. The predicate is also too weak in the other direction: it only excludes slots that end at or before the window start or start after the window end, so a slot that starts before the window and ends inside it is treated as bookable. Availability should require the whole slot to sit inside at least one same-day window.

Override date match depends on the server timezone

Whether an override applies is decided by comparing dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") to slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD"). slotStartTime is time.utc(), so its format is UTC. The left side is built with dayjs(date.start) in local mode, so format uses the Node process timezone. If that timezone is not UTC, an override whose shifted instant falls on a different local calendar date than its UTC date does not match the slot. US evening overrides, which land in the 00:00–04:00Z window, are the typical case: dateOverrideExist stays false and the override is silently ignored, so the fixed host is treated as on their normal hours. Both sides need to be formatted in UTC, or the day bounds compared as absolute instants.

Override timezone conversion drops the day and double-applies DST

Date overrides are stored as the organizer's wall-clock time encoded in a UTC timestamp (a 14:00 IST override is 14:00Z, which the existing tests rely on). The new code adds inviteeOffset − organizerOffset minutes and then keeps only .hour() and .minute(), so a result on the previous or next calendar day cannot be represented. A 20:00–23:00 organizer-UTC override viewed from UTC+3 becomes 23:00 and 02:00; end-minute 120 is less than start-minute 1380, buildSlots drops any range whose start is not before its end, and the host's normal hours for that day were already removed, so the attendee sees no slots instead of 23:00–02:00. A Tokyo 08:00 override is placed at 19:00 on the New York day that contains the raw 08:00Z value, which is the next New York date, not 19:00 the previous evening (the real instant, 08:00 JST). Those minutes are then passed through buildSlots's organizerDSTDiff − inviteeDSTDiff correction, which exists for values computed from today's offset; these minutes already used the offset at the override instant, so when the two zones are not in the same DST period versus today every override slot shifts by an extra hour. Offsets are read via dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone): Date#toString is implementation-defined, a failed parse yields NaN and the range is dropped, and a missing timeZone (optional on TimeRange) throws from .tz() and fails the whole schedule request. checkIfIsAvailable converts the same overrides a different way (subtract the organizer offset and compare absolute instants), so the two layers disagree and a cross-midnight override can be emitted by one and rejected by the other, blanking the day.

Fixed-host override behavior is untested

The only new assertion re-queries the same personal event — one host, one override window, no calendar busy time — in Asia/Dhaka and expects the same UTC instants as Asia/Kolkata. That does not cover fixed-host round-robin, which is the bug the PR says it fixes, nor two windows on one date, a blocked day (start equal to end), a busy conflict on an override day, a timezone gap that crosses midnight, or a DST boundary. createBookingScenario never attaches hosts to the mocked event type, and the host fixture is not the { isFixed, user } shape getSchedule reads, so the new fixed-host branch of checkIfIsAvailable cannot be exercised without harness changes. The new paths can drop all slots or ignore busy times while this test stays green.

On the next run of this SMS cron, any row with retryCount greater than 1 is deleted, including email and WhatsApp reminders and SMS rows already marked scheduled with a Twilio referenceId. Deleting a scheduled row drops the referenceId used to cancel the queued text, so a later booking cancellation cannot stop the message. The comment above the query still says it only removes past SMS reminders, which is no longer true. Scope the retry branch to unscheduled SMS (method SMS and scheduled false).

false_positives.candidate:
Two failures of any kind permanently drop the SMS

retryCount is incremented both when scheduleSMS returns a falsy value and for every exception in the surrounding try, including template rendering, getBookerBaseUrl, and database lookups, not only Twilio rejections. The next cron then deletes the row once retryCount > 1. Permanent failures (invalid number) and transient ones (Twilio 5xx, rate limit, network, brief DB error) share that budget, with no backoff beyond the cron interval. Two failures close together therefore remove the reminder even if the event is still days away, so a short provider outage can silently drop every SMS reminder in the 7-day window. Only non-retryable errors should exhaust the counter; transient errors need more attempts or a delay before deletion.

Missing number or empty body never consumes retries

retryCount is only updated when scheduleSMS returns falsy or throws. If sendTo is missing or the message body is empty, the code skips the send and does not increment retryCount or delete the row. Those reminders stay scheduled=false and are loaded, and their templates rebuilt, on every cron run until scheduledDate is in the past. That is the unbounded retry this PR is meant to stop, for a permanent failure that will never succeed. Treat that skip as a failed attempt or delete the row.

Retry-count update in catch aborts the rest of the batch

The new workflowReminder.update inside the per-reminder catch is not guarded. If it throws — the row was already deleted because the booking was cancelled, or the database errors — the exception escapes the catch, the original scheduling error is never logged, and the for-loop stops. Every later reminder in this invocation is skipped. Previously a single reminder failure was logged and the handler continued. If scheduleSMS had already accepted the message and the follow-up update failed, this path also counts that as a retry failure without saving referenceId, so the queued text can no longer be cancelled. The retry update needs its own try/catch so one row cannot fail the batch.

retryCount cleanup sequentially scans WorkflowReminder

Every cron invocation deletes rows with retryCount > 1, but the new predicate is not covered by the existing indexes on (method, scheduled, scheduledDate), bookingUid, workflowStepId, seatReferenceId, or (cancelled, scheduledDate). Postgres must sequentially scan WorkflowReminder on each run, even when almost no rows match. On a bookings-scale table that scan is repeated for the life of the cron. Add an index that matches the cleanup filter (for example method plus retryCount) if this delete stays.

No test locks the retry delete scope or threshold

The PR adds a destructive delete and a failure counter with no tests. Nothing asserts that an email or WhatsApp reminder with retryCount > 1 is kept, that an already scheduled SMS row is kept, that a missing phone number does not spin until the event date, or that an SMS reminder is removed only after two failures and not on the first. Those are the branches this change gets wrong, and a fixture test of the delete filter and the increment paths would have caught them.

OR SQL fragments are unsafe to AND with more predicates

Team and org authorization SQL is an OR of a team-booking predicate and a personal-booking predicate, joined as `(${left}) OR (${right})` in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition. That groups each side only; it does not parenthesize the whole OR. When eventTypeId and memberUserId are absent, getBaseConditions returns that fragment unchanged. SQL binds AND tighter than OR, so a caller query `WHERE ${conditions} AND "startTime" >= ${from}` is parsed as team-booking-predicate OR (personal-booking-predicate AND startTime >= from). Every team booking for an authorized team is included even when it fails the date range or any other AND predicate the caller adds. The event-type filter has the same shape, `("eventTypeId" = id) OR ("eventParentId" = id)`, with no outer parentheses. Interpolating it as `WHERE ${auth} AND ${eventTypeFilter}` is parsed as (auth AND eventTypeId = id) OR (eventParentId = id), so any booking whose parent event type matches is returned even if authorization fails. getBaseConditions does wrap both sides when a filter is present, but the no-filter return value and the public getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions fragments are not embed-safe. The old Prisma where-objects were grouped by the query engine, so this is a regression of the raw-SQL conversion. Wrap every fragment in an outer pair of parentheses before returning it.

Prisma.sql toEqual checks do not match nested fragments

The team-scope assertion here, the org-scope assertion around line 332, and the combined-filter assertion around line 429 expect a single flat Prisma.sql template via toEqual. The service builds those conditions with Array.reduce, nesting Prisma.sql fragments, and Prisma.sql does not flatten nested fragments until execution. The actual object has inner Sql values; the expected object has raw ids and arrays in values. Deep equality fails even when the SQL text and parameters match, so these tests fail in CI and do not validate authorization or filter SQL. Compare a flattened statement and parameter list, or execute the SQL.

Team and org authorization SQL is never executed

The only database query in this file is the user-scope getBaseConditions case, which is userId equality AND teamId IS NULL. Team and org authorization, including teamId/userId = ANY(array) and the isTeamBooking OR groups, are only compared as objects. PostgreSQL array binding for Prisma raw parameters and AND/OR precedence are therefore untested. Execute those fragments with $queryRaw against rows that must be included and rows that must be excluded (another org's team, a non-member personal booking, a team booking versus a personal booking, and an extra AND predicate such as a date range).
