SendGrid will not cancel a scheduled send less than 10 minutes before sendAt. If the booking is cancelled after the last cron run that is still more than 10 minutes before send time, the next run either happens after scheduledDate — and that job first deletes every EMAIL reminder with scheduledDate <= now, so cancel is never attempted — or SendGrid rejects the late cancel. The reminder is delivered. This is the common case of cancelling shortly before a reminder. Deferral also does not protect the 100-cap for sends already inside the one-hour window, because those cancellations would be pending for under an hour either way. Reminders already inside that window should be cancelled immediately; only later sends should be flagged for the cron.

Past-due reminders are deleted before SendGrid cancellation is attempted

The cron starts by deleting every EMAIL WorkflowReminder with scheduledDate <= now, including rows with cancelled=true, and only then loads reminders to cancel (lines 44-51). The row is the only copy of the SendGrid batch id. If an earlier run did not cancel that batch (downtime, a thrown cancel aborting the loop, or the booking being cancelled after the last pre-send run), SendGrid still has the scheduled mail and this delete makes a later cancel impossible. Past-due cleanup must not remove cancelled rows until a SendGrid cancel has been attempted and the outcome recorded. As written, any missed window permanently fails the fix.

One SendGrid cancel failure aborts the rest and skips DB cleanup

remindersToCancel is handled in a single try/catch. Each POST is awaited in order, and the prisma deletes are only executed after every request succeeds. Any rejection — the 100 pending-cancellation cap, SendGrid refusing a cancel inside its 10-minute cutoff, a null referenceId, or a network error — jumps to the catch, which only logs, then the handler goes on to schedule new mail. Later reminders in that run are not cancelled. Rows whose POST already succeeded are not deleted, so the next run must redo them. A row that fails every time stays in the result set until its scheduledDate passes and the earlier deleteMany removes it, and each run that hits it aborts the rest of the batch, so those other cancelled reminders are sent. The query also does not require method EMAIL or a non-null referenceId, so one bad row is enough to fail the POST. Handle each reminder independently, skip rows without a batch id, and delete a row only after its own cancel succeeds.

Paid booking cancellation returns before workflow reminders are cancelled

If the booking is paid, this branch refunds, sets status to REJECTED, and returns "Booking successfully cancelled." before the reminder block at line 484. That block is the only place this handler marks email reminders cancelled or deletes SMS reminders. The earlier return null when the payment app is missing (around line 437) skips it too. Paid event types can still have workflows, and bookingToDelete already loads workflowReminders, but they are ignored on this path. A cancelled paid booking therefore keeps its scheduled emails and SMS. If the reminder was not yet handed to SendGrid, the cron's unscheduled query does not check booking status and will schedule and send it; if it was already scheduled, the cron only cancels rows with cancelled=true, which was never set. Reminder cancellation has to run on this path before returning.

Every workflow save recreates reminders while old SendGrid batches stay live

An existing step is treated as edited when JSON.stringify(oldStep) !== JSON.stringify(newStep). oldStep is a Prisma WorkflowStep and always includes numberVerificationPending; newStep is the zod input and has senderName instead, so the comparison is always true even when nothing changed. The branch used to delete the WorkflowReminder row; that deleteMany was removed. It now only calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder (line 576), which sets cancelled and leaves the SendGrid scheduled send in place, and that call is not awaited. The same request then scheduleEmailReminder's a new batch for every future booking of that step. Every workflow save therefore leaves the previous batches live until the cron's one-hour window and adds another set. Near-term reminders can be delivered twice. All superseded batches become pending cancellations in the same hour, which can exceed SendGrid's 100-cap and cause the cron cancel loop to fail. Compare the actual editable fields, and do not create the replacement send until the previous batch is flagged or cancelled.

No tests for deferred cancel or the cron SendGrid cancellation loop

The PR replaces SendGrid cancellation and adds a cron path, but no test covers deleteScheduledEmailReminder, the cancelled flag, reschedule/workflow-delete behavior, or the scheduleEmailReminders cancellation loop. The previous fix used the wrong SendGrid endpoint and failed in production once 100 pending cancellations accumulated. Without a test that a far-future cancel only sets cancelled, that an imminent cancel actually stops the batch, and that one failed POST does not skip the remaining rows, the same production failure can regress unnoticed.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive

BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS values are lowercased but not trimmed, and the submitted address is not trimmed or lowercased before includes(). A blocked address with different casing, or a blacklist entry with a leading space after the comma, is stored and emailed. Duplicate detection uses case-sensitive equality, so A@x.com and a@x.com both become Attendee rows, and the organizer's own email is not excluded. The read of existing attendees is also outside a transaction, so two parallel requests can both pass the filter and insert the same guest. Normalize both sides with trim and lowercase, trim blacklist entries, and do not add the organizer as an attendee. Mixed requests currently drop blocked or duplicate addresses silently and still return success.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies that blacklist entries are lowercased while submitted guest emails are not, allowing blocked addresses to bypass the includes() check through different casing. This matches the golden issue despite additional concerns.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Team admin/owner check can never succeed

isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner. Membership role is a single value, so a user is never both ADMIN and OWNER, and the && short-circuits. If isTeamAdmin matches only ADMIN, the check is always false; if it also treats OWNER as admin, only owners pass and admins still fail. Either way team admins cannot add guests unless they are also the booking organizer or an attendee, which contradicts the variable name and the permission gate. The bookings UI still shows Additional guests on confirmed rows, so those users hit FORBIDDEN. Use ||, and skip the lookup when eventType.teamId is null instead of querying team id 0.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same incorrect use of && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner and recommends || so either role grants permission. Its additional lookup concern does not change this match.

true_positives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Already-invited emails get a new booking confirmation

sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw guests input, not uniqueGuests, the addresses actually inserted. In that helper, any attendee whose email is in the list receives AttendeeScheduledEmail (a full new-booking confirmation with cancel and reschedule links) instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. If the request includes someone already on the booking plus a new guest, the existing person is not inserted again but still gets a fresh scheduled email and does not get the guests-added notice. The includes() check is also case-sensitive. Pass the normalized list of addresses that were actually added.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same recipient-classification bug in sendAddGuestsEmails: it iterates over all calendarEvent attendees and uses membership in the raw input guests array to choose AttendeeScheduledEmail versus AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, potentially misclassifying existing attendees as newly added guests.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Add-guest emails ignore disabled standard emails

sendAddGuestsEmails always emails the organizer and every attendee. Other helpers in this file (sendScheduledEmails, sendLocationChangeEmails, sendCancelledEmails, and the rest) skip host or attendee mail when event-type metadata disables standard emails. This helper has no such check, and addGuestsHandler never passes eventType.metadata. Organizers who turned those emails off still get guest-added mail and full AttendeeScheduledEmail messages, including ICS and meeting links, when guests are added. Pass the metadata through and honor the same disable flags.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify that sendAddGuestsEmails fails to honor the EventType metadata disableStandardEmails flags, causing host and attendee emails to be sent even when disabled.

false_positives.candidate:
Calendar update uses the caller's credentials

EventManager is built from the signed-in user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). Calendar BookingReferences are tied to the organizer's credential id (and other hosts' credentials on collective events), not the caller's. The query already loads booking.user with credentials and destinationCalendar and never uses that user. When an attendee adds guests, the host calendar event is not updated. On collective events, other hosts' calendar copies cannot be updated either because only one user's credentials are supplied. Load decrypted credentials for the booking organizer (getUsersCredentials, not the raw Prisma credential rows) and include collective hosts.

Any attendee can invite unlimited guests on any booking

Authorization only checks organizer, attendee, or the broken team-admin flag. booking.status, end time, and list size are never validated, and ZAddGuestsInputSchema is an unbounded email array. Any logged-in attendee can therefore add as many addresses as they want to a cancelled, rejected, unconfirmed, or past booking. Each new address is sent AttendeeScheduledEmail, and the mailer hardcodes ICS status CONFIRMED. videoCallData (join URL and meeting password) is copied onto the event whenever a video reference exists, so those invites disclose meeting access for events that are not accepted upcoming meetings, and a participant can send unlimited calendar mail through the platform. Restrict this to accepted future bookings and cap the guest list.

Seated events are not capacity-checked

Guests are inserted as Attendee rows with no comparison to eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot, which is only copied onto the calendar payload later. If occupancy is the attendee count, this overbooks the slot and can block real bookers. If occupancy is BookingSeat / seatsReferences, these guests become attendees with no seat, so seat counts, the seats UI, and cancel/reschedule links diverge from the attendee list. seatsShowAttendees is also ignored: sendAddGuestsEmails and the ICS include every attendee, leaking participant emails on events configured to hide them. Enforce remaining capacity before insert, or reject add-guests for seated events, and honor seatsShowAttendees when emailing.

Guests stay saved when calendar or email updates fail

prisma.booking.update commits the new Attendee rows before translation loading, updateCalendarAttendees, and sendAddGuestsEmails. The calendar call is outside the try/catch, so a thrown calendar or translation error returns 500 after the insert. A retry then filters those addresses out as already present and throws emails_must_be_unique_valid, so the calendar update and invite emails are never retried and the user is told the addresses are invalid. Email failures are caught, logged as a static string with the error discarded, and the handler still returns success, so the dialog toasts Guests added when nobody was notified. Roll back or make the side effects retryable, and do not report success when notification failed.

New guests are stored with a blank name

Every newly inserted guest is saved with name set to an empty string. Scheduled and add-guest mail payloads address the recipient as `${attendee.name} <${attendee.email}>`, so new guests, who are sent AttendeeScheduledEmail, get a blank display name (` <email>`). The same empty name is sent in the calendar attendee update. Use the email address, or its local part, when no name was collected.

Collective co-hosts are never notified

The CalendarEvent built for notifications never sets team or team.members, even though eventType is already loaded. sendAddGuestsEmails only emails extra hosts when calendarEvent.team.members is present, so that loop never runs. On a collective event, only booking.user receives OrganizerAddGuestsEmail; the other hosts are not told that guests were added. Load the event-type hosts and set calEvent.team the same way other booking mail flows do.

Add-guests is offered on past bookings

The new additional-guests action is added to editBookingActions, which is included in bookedActions. bookedActions is not limited to upcoming meetings: past confirmed bookings and past pending bookings also render TableActions with that list. Using it still inserts attendees and sends AttendeeScheduledEmail plus an ICS REQUEST for a time that already passed. Only show this action for accepted upcoming bookings, and enforce the same rule in addGuestsHandler.

No tests for addGuests authorization or failure paths

The new mutation ships with no unit or integration tests. The inverted team-admin condition, access to cancelled or past bookings, seated overbooking, blacklist casing, and a calendar or email failure after the attendee insert would not be caught in CI. Cover organizer, team admin, team owner, attendee, and stranger; non-accepted bookings; seat capacity; and a side-effect failure after insert.

false_negatives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup code comparison is case-sensitive and unnormalized

Codes are generated as lowercase hex (crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex") in setup.ts) and login compares them with indexOf after only stripping "-". The same check is in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts at the backupCode.replaceAll call. There is no toLowerCase() or trim, and spaces are left in place. The recovery input in apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx uses placeholder "XXXXX-XXXXX" and does not set autoCapitalize="none", so mobile keyboards and anyone following the placeholder submit uppercase hex. Those attempts always fail as an incorrect backup code, which blocks the recovery path when the authenticator is already lost. Normalize by trimming, removing dashes and spaces, and lowercasing on the server, and stop advertising uppercase in the field.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same underlying bug: indexOf performs a case-sensitive comparison against lowercase hex backup codes, causing uppercase user input to fail validation. Its additional normalization and UI observations do not change the core match.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
One-time backup codes are consumed with a lost update

Redeeming a backup code decrypts the stored list, finds a match, sets that slot to null, and writes the whole blob back with a plain user.update keyed only by id. There is no transaction, row lock, or compare-and-swap on the previous ciphertext. Two overlapping logins can both read the same list and both succeed: the same code opens two sessions, and if the requests use two different codes the later write restores the code the earlier request consumed. The promise that each code works exactly once is therefore not enforced. Consume the code with a conditional update (or SELECT FOR UPDATE) that fails if backupCodes changed, and only then issue the session.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify a race condition in the read-decrypt-mutate-write flow that allows concurrent login requests to redeem the same backup code more than once, violating one-time-use semantics. The candidate also describes a related lost-update consequence.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup-code login skips the password when totpCode is set

Password verification runs only when `user.password` is set and `credentials.totpCode` is empty (the check around line 121). The new backup-code branch then logs the user in if the backup code matches and never validates `totpCode`. A request with the victim's email, any non-empty totpCode (for example "000000"), and a valid backup code therefore skips the password entirely, consumes that code, and creates a session. Backup codes are supposed to replace the authenticator only; the login UI still sends the password and clears totpCode, but the credentials callback must not trust the client to omit totpCode. Anyone who obtains a backup code (the downloaded cal-backup-codes.txt, a screenshot, a clipboard history) can take over the account without the password. Verify the password inside this branch whenever the user has one, and do not treat an unchecked totpCode as proof the password was already accepted.

Closing the codes dialog does not finish 2FA setup

On a successful enable response the modal only moves to DisplayBackupCodes and no longer calls onEnable(). onEnable() runs solely from the footer Close button. Escape, the overlay, and the dialog's default close control go through onOpenChange and do not notify the parent, so the settings switch stays off while twoFactorEnabled is already true on the server. Clicking the switch again calls setup and gets TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled, so the user cannot finish or disable 2FA until a full reload. The codes themselves exist only in component state and a blob URL from the earlier setup response; nothing can fetch or regenerate them. Refreshing, closing the tab, or dismissing the dialog drops the only copy. The copy button makes this worse: navigator.clipboard.writeText is not awaited, and the success toast is shown even if the write fails, so the user can close thinking the codes were saved. Call onEnable() when enable succeeds (and on every close after that), require an explicit save acknowledgement, and do not toast success unless the clipboard write resolves.

missing_backup_codes points at a settings flow that does not exist

The new string says "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." This PR only creates codes inside the initial 2FA setup response and never adds a settings action to generate or rotate them. Users who enabled 2FA before the migration, or who dismissed the one-time codes screen, hit this error on "Lost access" and are told to do something the product cannot do. They can only get codes by disabling 2FA (which still requires the authenticator) and turning it on again. The message should not claim a generate-in-settings flow unless that flow exists.

Tests never log in or disable 2FA with a backup code

The new coverage only clicks download, copy, and close on the codes screen. Nothing submits a backup code at login, checks that a used code is rejected, or disables 2FA with a backup code (the TODO at the top of this file calls that out). The existing enable-and-login test was not updated for the new screen: after OTP it never clicks backup-codes-close, and expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy() asserts on the Promise returned by isChecked(), which is always truthy, so it passes even when the switch is unchecked. A break in backup-code authentication, including the password bypass and the non-atomic consume, would not fail CI.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google Meet bookings crash when no destination calendar is set

The Cal Video fallback now does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no null check. If destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or [], that value is undefined and booking creation throws TypeError before the location can be switched. The old code used optional chaining, so Meet with no Google calendar fell back to Cal Video. Every caller that passes null or [] (new bookings with no destination calendar, confirmation, and payment webhooks) will 500 on Google Meet instead of booking.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same underlying null-reference bug: destructuring a null or empty destinationCalendar yields an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar, and accessing its integration property without a guard throws. Although it does not explicitly name both createEvent() and updateEvent(), the described cause matches the golden issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google update/delete fallback can never resolve a calendar id

updateEvent now does `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`. When externalCalendarId is null, undefined, or empty, the find compares every calendar id to that same falsy value and always returns undefined. The previous fallback was the destination calendar's externalId. calendar.events.update is then called with calendarId undefined and the update fails. deleteEvent (around line 315) uses the same dead find and then substitutes "primary", so a missing externalCalendarId deletes on the primary calendar; a 404 is treated as success and the event remains on the calendar it was actually created on. Any reference stored without externalCalendarId, including the no-credentialId create branch and seated-attendee updates that pass a null externalCalendarId, hits this.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the broken calendar lookup that compares cal.externalId to externalCalendarId instead of using an appropriate identifier such as credentialId. The candidate clarifies that the lookup occurs in the falsy-ID fallback and explains its update/delete consequences, but points to the same underlying logic error.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Organization slug condition is inverted

The organization create payload changed `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` into `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. That drops the negation. With billing disabled, neither `slug` nor `requestedSlug` is saved, so the new org has no URL. With billing enabled, `slug` is written immediately and `requestedSlug` is still written, so the slug is claimed before payment instead of staying pending. This is unrelated to destination calendars and will break org creation in both modes.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition for slug assignment and the same consequence: both slug and requestedSlug are set when billing is enabled, and neither is set when disabled.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
One missing host credential fails every calendar update

The new per-reference update loop loads a credential from the DB, but if that row is missing or has no app.slug it still pushes updateEvent(undefined, ...). getCalendar then rejects. Unlike createAllCalendarEvents, there is no `if (credential)` guard. The shared catch (around line 591) also dropped the console.error, and it returns a synthetic failure for every calendar reference instead of the updates that already succeeded. With multiple host references, one deleted or unlinked credential makes reschedule, location change, and attendee updates report total calendar failure and hides the underlying error. The seated-merge delete just below also calls getCalendar on a findUnique result with no null check, so a missing old credential aborts the same way.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same missing-credential bug: a failed credential lookup can cause updateEvent to receive undefined without a guard, resulting in a runtime failure. Its additional observations do not change this semantic match.

false_positives.candidate:
Secondary host events are created against the first destination calendar

createAllCalendarEvents loops over every destination calendar and calls createEvent once per host credential, but it still passes the full destinationCalendar array. CalendarManager.createEvent forwards only credential.id into the service, not that destination's externalId. Office 365, Lark, and CalDAV/Apple all still read only the first array element: Office builds `/me/calendars/${firstExternalId}/events` with the other host's token, Lark creates on the first calendar id, and BaseCalendarService filters to the first externalId. If that id is not on the secondary account, CalDAV's filter matches nothing, Promise.all of an empty list is treated as success, and a booking reference is stored for an event that was never created. Google does look up calendarId by credentialId, but the organizer attendee email is still the first destination's externalId, so the secondary Google insert can 400 or list the wrong organizer. Hosts other than the first therefore do not reliably get a calendar event, which is the bug this PR is meant to fix.

Collective host calendars are dropped when the organizer has none

Team destination calendars are collected for COLLECTIVE hosts, then attached with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)`. The evt is initialized to null when both the event type and the organizer have no destination calendar, so the optional push is a no-op and those host calendars are discarded. createAllCalendarEvents then takes the empty branch, whose fallback filters credentials with `type === "calendar"`. Real types are `google_calendar` and similar, so that fallback never matches either. A collective booking whose organizer has not set a destination calendar creates no per-host calendar events even when every other host has a calendar connected.

Cancelling remaining recurring bookings does not delete each host event

The new per-reference cancel loop wraps the recurring all-remaining branch unchanged. That branch ignores the reference it is iterating, loads only booking.user.credentials (the organizer, not other hosts, and with no DB lookup), and for each future instance deletes only the first reference whose type includes `_calendar`. Other hosts' events on those instances are never deleted, so their calendars keep the cancelled series. Because this sits inside the new for-loop, the same incomplete delete also runs once per calendar reference and hammers the first event. The non-recurring branch already deletes each reference with its own credentialId and a DB fallback; the recurring branch needs the same treatment over every updated instance's calendar references.

Payment and confirmation creates still use a single destination calendar

Only handleNewBooking appends the other collective hosts' destination calendars. Stripe payment_intent.succeeded calls EventManager.create with an evt whose destinationCalendar is at most `[booking.destinationCalendar || user.destinationCalendar]`. The same single-calendar evt is built in getBooking (used by setup_intent.succeeded around the eventManager.create call) and in paypal-webhook.ts handlePaymentSuccess. confirm.handler.ts builds the same one-element list from the booking relation or the session user and passes it to handleConfirmation, without loading event-type hosts. Booking.destinationCalendar can store only the first calendar (handleNewBooking connects evt.destinationCalendar[0]). Paid or requires-confirmation collective bookings therefore still create only the organizer's calendar event, so the other hosts never get invited.

Video booking references no longer store credentialId

referencesToCreate used to set credentialId to result.credentialId for every non-calendar result. It is now `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so video (and any other non-calendar) references are always saved without a credential id. handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when bookingVideoReference.credentialId is set, and then looks that id up in the user's credentials. New bookings will leave Zoom/Daily/other video meetings in place on cancel, and later location updates cannot find the credential that created the meeting.

Location updates persist calendar references without ids

updateLocation now sets externalCalendarId from result.externalId and credentialId from result.credentialId only. CalendarManager.updateEvent does not return either field, and the previous fallbacks to evt.destinationCalendar.externalId and credentialId were removed. editLocation writes referencesToCreate onto the booking. Calendar update results have updatedEvent rather than createdEvent, so those new rows also get uid "". A later cancel treats them as legacy references and calls deleteEvent with an empty uid on every calendar credential, and the real calendar id needed to patch the existing event is gone.

CRM other_calendar references are updated twice

calendar references are now every reference whose type includes `_calendar`. Types such as closecom_other_calendar match that filter, so they are updated in the new per-reference loop and again by the later pass that filters `type.includes("other_calendar")`. Previously find() handled only the first calendar reference, and the second pass was what updated CRM calendars. Duplicate updates can create duplicate CRM activities or fail the second call. The first loop should exclude other_calendar types.

Seat merge deletes only the first host calendar event

When newBookingId is set (rescheduling a seated attendee into an existing slot), the cleanup still does booking.references.find for a single `_calendar` reference and deletes only that event. The rest of this function was rewritten to walk every calendar reference, but this path was not. Other hosts keep a live event at the old time after the merge, so their calendars stay busy and still show the meeting.

Webhook destinationCalendar shape changed and is inconsistent

CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from a single DestinationCalendar or null to an array or null, and that object is spread into webhook payloads. Subscribers reading destinationCalendar.integration or destinationCalendar.externalId will break, but the PR is marked as a non-breaking bug fix. Emitters also disagree on the empty value: handleNewBooking still sends null when no calendar is set, while confirm, cancel, reminders, and payment handlers send []. The e2e suite only changed BOOKING_REJECTED to expect [] and still expects null for BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED, so the new contract is neither documented nor consistently tested.

No test covers multi-host calendar create or cancel

This change rewrites create, update, and delete across every destination calendar, but the only test edit is an e2e webhook expectation for an empty destinationCalendar. There is no coverage that a collective booking writes one event per host credential, that Google Meet with no destination calendar still books, that Office/CalDAV/Apple hosts are not given the organizer's calendar id, or that cancelling all remaining recurring instances deletes every host event. The PR checklist notes that no such tests were added, so these regressions will not be caught before merge.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

true_positives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

Reschedule cleanup uses forEach(async) and never finishes

This is a regression from the async app-store change: previously getCalendar was synchronous, so deleteEvent was at least invoked before the callback yielded, and deleteMeeting started the provider call before returning. true_positives.matched_candidate:

Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, i.e. SpawnProcess. The new guard therefore never calls kill() in _ensure_processes_alive, and the same check in join() never calls terminate(). Previously kill() was unconditional, so this is a regression on the default single-process path as well as the multi-process path. A hung worker is left running, the restart counter is incremented, and _create_process_for_shards overwrites self.processes and drops the only reference the strategy keeps. The orphan keeps calling flush_segments/produce/done_flush_segments on the same shards as the replacement, which can duplicate segments on the buffered-segments topic or delete Redis state the other worker is still producing. The replacement also resets process_healthy_since, so once it looks healthy the parent stops retrying and the orphan runs until the consumer process exits. join() likewise cannot SIGTERM a worker blocked in Redis or Kafka that never observes the stopped flag. Thread-mode restarts (produce_to_pipe) leak the same way because nothing stops the previous thread. Even after the type check is fixed (use BaseProcess, or skip only threading.Thread), kill() is asynchronous and the replacement is started immediately with no join; the old worker must be reaped before a new one is started.

true_positives.golden_comment: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
true_positives.matched_candidate:

join() sets a deadline, spends the full timeout in next_step.join(timeout), then walks flusher workers. If the deadline is already exhausted it breaks immediately; if it expires mid-loop the break skips every remaining worker. Those workers are neither waited on nor terminated. close() intentionally does not stop flushers (to avoid a Redis memory spike at rebalance start), so join() is the only shutdown barrier. A worker blocked in flush_segments or Kafka produce will not see stopped until that call returns, and after the break nothing signals it. Kafka rebalance then builds a new SpanFlusher for the same shards — in this process or another — while the old workers are still flushing, so both produce the same segments and race on Redis flush markers. The previous single-process join always fell through to terminate() after the wait; the early break is a regression. On the way out of join(), every worker that is still alive must be killed and joined, including when the timeout is already spent.

The lookup therefore uses the generic project default stats window rather than the replay's own start/end. Give the list container flex: 1 and min-height: 0 (and overflow: hidden) so it fills only the space under the summary.

useTraceItemAttributeKeys used to always reduce the API payload to a TagCollection (empty object if data was missing) and return that once loading finished. It now returns useQuery's data directly: attributes is previous while isFetching, otherwise data. On error, isFetching is false and data is undefined, and there is no ?? {}. Explore callers that wait for !isLoading and then spread or Object.keys the result will throw, blanking the search builder, instead of seeing an empty tag set. The feedback list on the same page is scoped by the environment page filter. With an environment selected, the summary is computed from every environment in the projects and date range, so it can describe feedback the list is not showing.
